docs.title: Risk-Based Inspection and Corrosion Management Practice
docs.author: Rochelle Mark — Inspection Engineer
docs.reviewers: Wayne Rajkumar — Inspection Lead; Sophia de Souza — Materials & Corrosion Lead; Allison Mitchell — Pipelines Lead; Marlon Gonzales — Static Mechanical Lead
docs.applies: PAP, CHB, SAP, CPF, LND, PLB
docs.subtitle: Method for assessing degradation, planning inspection, managing corrosion and dispositioning anomalies.

blocks.t: This Practice establishes ACE’s method for risk-based inspection (RBI), corrosion management and anomaly disposition. It supports the Asset Integrity Management Standard; it does not replace asset-specific engineering design, inspection procedures, statutory examinations or repair engineering.
Applies to pressure equipment, piping, pipelines, tanks, structures and integrity-managed equipment at CPF, Pommerac A, Chenet B, Sapodilla C, land leases and associated export systems.

The Practice defines mechanism screening, risk ranking, inspection strategy, monitoring, pipeline integrity, deferral, anomaly assessment and records. Site inspection plans and work packs implement the method.

Parent Standard: ACE-AIM-STD-001 Asset Integrity Management Standard sets what must be true for asset integrity. This Practice sets how ACE inspects, monitors and dispositions degradation so that those requirements are met. It applies at PAP, CHB, SAP, CPF, LND and PLB.

Recognised practice applied: API RP 580 Risk-Based Inspection; API RP 581 Risk-Based Inspection Methodology; API RP 584 Integrity Operating Windows; API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 Fitness-For-Service; API RP 1160 Managing System Integrity for Hazardous Liquid Pipelines; NACE SP0169 Control of External Corrosion on Underground or Submerged Metallic Piping Systems.

Inspection Engineer develops RBI inputs, scope, packages and results. Inspection Lead reviews programme quality, intervals, risk rankings and deferrals. Materials & Corrosion Lead owns damage mechanism and corrosion method decisions. Pipelines Lead owns pipeline strategy. Static Mechanical Lead provides pressure-equipment and fitness-for-service input. Operations supplies history, access, safe state and operating restrictions.
Technical decisions are referred to the relevant Technical Authority and delegated approval structure. Process ownership does not transfer technical accountability.

rows: Approves the method and its revisions; resolves conflicts between production and integrity priorities.
Maintains the method, the inspection programme quality and the deferral register.
Sophia de Souza — Materials & Corrosion Lead
Damage mechanism screening, inhibitor objectives, corrosion rate methods.
Pipeline threat assessment, ILI and CP strategy, pipeline anomaly disposition.
Pressure equipment, fitness-for-service and repair acceptance.
RBI inputs, inspection scopes, results evaluation and anomaly records.

blocks.t: The Inspection Lead shall maintain the site inspection programmes, the RBI register and the deferral register, and shall report their status to the Technical Leadership Council each quarter.
The Materials & Corrosion Lead shall approve the damage mechanism screening for every corrosion loop and every change to a corrosion inhibitor objective.

A technical decision on interval extension, deferral, fitness-for-service or return to service shall be approved by the Technical Authority named for that equipment class, and the decision record shall name the approver (C-AIM-010).
Define loops/circuits by process conditions, fluid composition, materials, geometry, flow regime and credible degradation. Boundaries and equipment identifiers must be stable and traceable.

Screen for CO₂ corrosion, H₂S-related damage, MIC, erosion/erosion-corrosion, CUI, atmospheric corrosion, galvanic effects, under-deposit corrosion, cracking, coating degradation and external corrosion as relevant.
Record susceptibility, expected morphology, locations, detection limitations, mitigation and consequence. Reassess when chemistry, conditions, material or inspection evidence changes.

Each corrosion loop shall have a documented damage mechanism screening that is reviewed at least every five years and after any change in fluid composition, operating conditions or materials (C-AIM-002).

Use the ACE Risk Matrix. Assess probability of failure (PoF) and consequence of failure (CoF); document dominant contributors, confidence, data quality and assumptions. RBI informs prioritisation and scope but does not override statutory or TA-approved constraints.

PoF considers mechanism, susceptibility, corrosion rate, wall loss/cracking, prior findings, inspection effectiveness, uncertainty and operating history. CoF considers people, environment, production, escalation, asset impact, location and repair complexity.
Record category, recommended actions and sensitivity where uncertainty could alter the ranking. Reassess after incidents, changes, new mechanisms or findings that invalidate assumptions.
Every integrity-managed item shall hold a current RBI assessment, no older than five years, traceable to its data sources, assumptions and approver (C-AIM-001).

Example: on the Pommerac A crude export line, the dominant PoF contributor is internal CO₂ corrosion at low points, and the CoF is driven by environmental release to the Gulf of Paria. Both contributors, and the confidence in the corrosion rate, are stated in the RBI record.
Set intervals from risk, degradation rate, confidence, inspection effectiveness, remaining life and mandatory constraints. Record the limiting basis and calculation assumptions.

Condition-based inspection requires validated, repeatable data. Fixed intervals are retained where mechanism uncertainty, consequence, data quality or monitoring limitations justify them. Intervals cannot exceed statutory, code or delegated technical limits.

Every inspection interval shall record its limiting basis (risk, remaining life, statutory or code limit) and the calculation used, and shall not exceed half the calculated remaining life (C-AIM-003).

rows: 1 year or 0.25 × remaining life, whichever is less
Only with TA approval and validated monitoring data

blocks.t: Define inhibitor objective, chemistry, injection point, delivery reliability, operating window, verification and response to under-delivery. Evidence must demonstrate delivery and effectiveness in the protected system.
Select coupons and probes for representative mechanisms and locations. Record exposure, retrieval, lab method, quality, corrosion rate, interpretation and discrepancies with other evidence.

Corrosion rate and remaining-life calculations use approved methods and validated data; include units, uncertainty, minimum required thickness and assumptions. Link to ACE-OPS-PRA-001 IOWs. Sustained low inhibitor delivery or exceedance is an integrity signal.

Corrosion inhibitor delivery shall be verified against its integrity operating window in ACE-OPS-PRA-001 at least weekly, and any sustained under-delivery shall be raised to the Materials & Corrosion Lead within 24 hours (C-AIM-005).

Integrate intelligent pigging, external corrosion protection, cathodic protection (CP), patrols, leak detection, operating data and repair history. Threat assessment determines the combination and frequency.
ILI frequency considers threat, previous results, growth, tool capability, access, uncertainty, operating condition and mandatory requirements. Deferrals require assessment and interim safeguards.

CP surveys, coating condition, test points and rectifier performance are reviewed together. Patrols complement instrumented inspection and do not replace it. Define patrol scope, observations and escalation thresholds. Suspected leaks are immediately communicated to Operations and the integrity owner.
Each pipeline shall have an integrity plan that sets ILI, CP survey and patrol frequencies from its threat assessment, reviewed annually by the Pipelines Lead (C-AIM-006).

rows: Per threat assessment; not more than 5 years for export lines

sections.title: 8 Deferral, anomalies and fitness for service

blocks.t: SCE inspection deferral requires documented risk assessment, TA approval, time limit, safeguards and ONE tracking. It does not reset the due date.

Anomaly records include finding, location, mechanism, severity, uncertainty, immediate controls, owner, due date and disposition. Operations applies conservative restrictions while integrity is uncertain.

Use recognised fitness-for-service methods such as API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 where applicable. Document assessment scope, input quality, limitations, criteria and authority. Disposition may be repair, replacement, monitoring, restriction or shutdown. Return to service requires verification and recorded release.

An inspection of a Safety Critical Element shall only be deferred with a documented risk assessment, TA approval, interim safeguards and an expiry date, and the deferral shall be visible in ONE until closed (C-AIM-004).
Every anomaly shall have a risk ranking, a named owner, a due date and closure evidence recorded in the anomaly register (C-AIM-007).
Do not reset the due date of a deferred inspection. The original due date stays on the record so that overdue time remains visible.

Link RBI, inspection scope, method limitations, results, thickness readings, corrosion rates, ILI, CP, monitoring, anomaly assessment, FFS, deferrals, repair and close-out to equipment ID, loop, location, anomaly ID and governing document.
Records must be searchable, attributable, revision controlled and retrievable. Use stable identifiers and reconcile missing or duplicate data before relying on it for risk decisions.
Inspection and monitoring data shall be validated by the Inspection Engineer before it is used in an RBI, interval or fitness-for-service decision (C-AIM-008).
Inspection results, corrosion rates, deferrals and anomaly dispositions shall be recorded in the CMMS against the equipment ID and retained for the life of the asset.

Inspection Lead reviews programme completion, overdue inspections, deferrals, high-risk anomalies, repeat findings and data quality. Materials & Corrosion Lead reviews corrosion-loop and inhibitor-monitoring effectiveness. Assurance samples traceability from mechanism and risk to inspection, disposition, work order and verified closure.
The Inspection Lead shall review programme completion, overdue inspections, deferrals and repeat damage every quarter and record the actions raised (C-AIM-009).

Leading: SCE inspections completed on time (target ≥ 95%); deferrals open past expiry (target 0); inhibitor availability within IOW (target ≥ 95%). Lagging: loss of containment from internal corrosion (target 0); repeat anomalies on the same loop.

rows: RBI, scope, preparation, field execution, results and close-out
Triage, safeguards, assessment, disposition, repair, verification

blocks.t: Each control below is written as an ODS.RiskControl statement in the section shown and is held in the Controls Register (ACE-RSK-REG-002) under the same Control ID.

rows: RBI assessment is current and traceable
SCE deferral has expiry and safeguards
Pipeline ILI, CP and patrol strategy is reviewed
Anomaly has risk, owner and closure evidence
Inspection data is validated and linked
Programme and repeat damage are reviewed

docs.title: Asset Integrity Management Standard
docs.author: Garvin Mark — Integrity Engineer
docs.reviewers: Marc Gomes — Maintenance & Integrity Manager; Wayne Rajkumar — Inspection Lead; Sophia de Souza — Materials & Corrosion Lead; Elena Farfan — Manager, Technical Excellence
docs.func: Engineering & Projects / Asset Integrity and Inspection
docs.applies: ACE offshore platforms and pipelines, land leases, wells, CPF, Point Lisas Shore Base, structures, plant and contracted interfaces under ACE control
docs.subtitle: Company-wide requirements for design integrity, safety-critical barriers, inspection, maintenance, anomaly control and independent verification throughout asset life.

blocks.t: ACE uses an integrated asset integrity management programme to ensure that facilities, wells, pipelines, structures, equipment and their protective functions remain fit for intended service throughout the life cycle. Technical integrity is established by an adequate design and verified construction; operating integrity is sustained by controlled limits, inspection, preventive maintenance, competent operation, anomaly management and verified barriers.

This standard defines the corporate minimum for identifying critical equipment, establishing performance requirements, implementing assurance activities, managing evidence of degradation, controlling impairment, accepting residual risks and learning from failures. It connects safety-case assumptions and hazard studies directly to the equipment, people and work activities intended to control them.

All assets and safety-critical elements operated by ACE shall have an accountable owner, a current technical basis, an appropriate integrity assurance plan and retrievable evidence of performance against that plan.

The portfolio includes Pommerac A, Chenet B and Sapodilla C in the Gulf of Paria, subsea export lines and associated risers, Tamarind, Pawpaw and Soursop land leases, the Central Processing Facility and its tank farm/jetty, Point Lisas Shore Base and relevant marine/logistics interfaces. Drilling and workover equipment are governed through contract assurance and the Wells system when operating on ACE’s behalf.

The programme covers pressure containment, rotating machinery, lifting and structural components, protective systems, electricity and automation, wells and subsurface barriers, pipelines and flowlines, corrosion protection, metering and safety systems. Commercial, maintainability and reliability concerns are included where failure creates unacceptable operational or integrity risk.

rows: Accountable for the engineering standards framework, technical integrity governance and assurance of the asset integrity management system.
Sets discipline requirements, arbitrates cross-discipline technical disputes and endorses standards, critical deviations and major integrity strategies.
Coordinates technical authority network, SCE register governance, escalations, deviations and assurance interfaces.
Maintains this standard, asset integrity strategy, common programme framework, major degradation risk visibility and consolidated reporting.
Delivers planned maintenance, condition monitoring, spares strategy and CMMS control for operating assets.
Sets inspection plans and quality requirements; challenges remaining-life assumptions and supports integrity risk screening.
Owns degradation mechanisms, corrosion loops, chemical treatment and materials selection technical review.
Owns site operating condition and immediate risk controls; stops or restricts operation with an impaired barrier.
Defines and endorses technical acceptance criteria, performance standards, deferrals and risk-reduction solutions.

sections.title: 1.4 One technical and operational risk thread

blocks.t: HAZID, HAZOP, LOPA and bow-tie analyses identify credible major accident hazards and required barriers. The ACE Risk Matrix sets corporate risk acceptance. Performance standards turn barrier expectations into measurable technical duties. CMMS and inspection programmes schedule and record assurance. Operating limits and Control of Work prevent operational conditions from invalidating credited protection; MOC ensures changes do not silently alter the barrier basis. Audits and incident learning update this chain.

Integrity requirements originating in hazard studies, performance standards and technical specifications shall be traceable to equipment identifiers, task records, acceptance criteria and an accountable ACE role.

Each operating asset or materially distinct asset grouping has an AIMP that consolidates integrity threats, engineering baselines, safety-critical functions, inspection and maintenance schemes, condition-monitoring plans, anomalies, ageing and life-extension risks, competence, interfaces, assurance and annual improvement actions. The plan is reviewed with the Area Authority and relevant TAs at least annually and following significant incidents or changes.

The asset owner shall maintain an AIMP linked to the risk register, critical equipment register and CMMS; changes in operating duty or credible damage mechanism require review of the AIMP before continued service is accepted.

sections.title: 1.6 Interfaces to contractors and shared systems

blocks.t: Contractor-operated equipment, leased packages, temporary generators, lifting appliances and marine systems are not exempt because they do not appear in ACE’s fixed-asset register. The accountable ACE manager identifies the contracted service boundaries, safety-critical duties, certification, inspection evidence, bridging, emergency interfaces, data return and escalation ownership. For shared facilities, joint venture and partner documentation must define the operator, asset owner and technical acceptance arrangements.
Maintain the interface register, bridging documents, vendor quality and verification records within the controlled repository with clear links to applicable asset and contract identifiers.

sections.title: 2.1 Identification of major accident hazard barriers

blocks.t: Safety-critical elements (SCEs) are physical, instrumented or operational elements whose failure could initiate, escalate or fail to mitigate a major accident. Identification starts with the major accident hazard inventory and bow-tie protection layers, not simply the most expensive or complicated equipment. The analysis covers prevention, detection, control and mitigation, including dependencies on utilities, software, instruments, human actions and supporting systems.

Each identified major accident hazard shall be mapped to its credited critical barriers and the SCEs needed to deliver their functions; the mapping shall be reviewed after significant design changes or incident learning.

rows: Pressure vessels, process piping, well barrier envelopes, ESD valves, isolation devices.
HAZOP/MAH scenario, containment boundary, test and inspection plan.
Fire and gas devices, shutdown sensors, logic solvers, emergency alarms.
Cause-and-effect, proof-test procedure, bypass control, associated utilities.
Pressure relief systems, blowdown, fireproofing, passive fire protection.
Relief/design basis, inspection/verification and loading assumptions.
Platform integrity, protective supports, critical moorings and access/egress elements.
Design loads, inspection basis, structural criticality and emergency routes.
Well barriers, downhole isolation, pipeline sectionalisation and leak detection.
Well/pipeline technical standards and test/inspection evidence.
Escape systems, emergency power, communications, firewater and evacuation support.
Emergency scenario, functionality and survivability criteria.

blocks.t: Not every equipment item within a barrier family is automatically an SCE. Discipline Technical Authorities determine the system boundary, function and dependencies for each asset and resolve classification disputes with the Process Safety Lead and Area Authority.

sections.title: 2.3 SCE register as the source of control

blocks.t: The SCE Register shall identify the unique SCE, related major accident hazards, credited function, asset boundary, technical owner, current performance standard, assurance tasks, condition and any open impairments or deviations.

rows: Unique identifier, location, subsystem and relevant equipment tags.
MAH, bow-tie or study ID; preventive or mitigation function.
Current performance standard revision, target criteria, critical dependencies.
TA, inspection/maintenance task IDs, proof-test or inspection status.
Healthy, impaired, unavailable, under repair; MOC/deviation and risk references.
Commissioning, modification, replacement, testing and verification references.
Latest evidence meets all approved performance criteria; within assurance interval.
Performance reduced or trending below a margin, but credited duty not demonstrably lost.
Assess within risk timescale; track anomaly and safeguards.
Cannot demonstrate all required criteria, or test is overdue without an approved deferral.
Record impairment, risk-assess, apply deviation and operating restrictions.
Required barrier does not function or has been intentionally bypassed.
Stop/restrict affected operation; escalate via Area Authority and TA.

blocks.t: A green maintenance schedule is not proof of barrier health when the function, test quality or actual degradation evidence fails its standard. Barrier health reflects verified functionality and critical dependencies.

The barrier map identifies common utilities, power, communications, instrument air, software, calibration, environment, operator response and shared components. Loss of one common service may disable several supposedly separate safeguards. Related alarms and maintenance findings are analysed together, not only as individual work orders.

No new or materially modified SCE performance requirement may be accepted without affected TA endorsement, Process Safety review where it protects a major accident scenario, and a documented path to periodic verification.

The performance standard (PS) turns a credited protective function into requirements that can be demonstrated in the field. It is the technical link between the risk assessment and maintenance/inspection actions. The PS includes the service conditions and design assumptions needed for an honest test of performance, together with meaningful pass/fail criteria.

Every SCE shall have a documented performance standard that states functionality, reliability or availability, survivability, dependencies, measurable acceptance criteria, verification method, frequency and accountable technical owner.

rows: Hazard addressed, initiation and target outcome; operating modes; system boundary.
Trip/action sequence, time to respond, sensing and control logic where applicable.
Target proof-test or inspection acceptance; diagnostic or failure-rate basis where applicable.
Credible fire, blast, flood, corrosion, impact or external conditions the element must withstand.
Flow, pressure, sealing, emergency power autonomy, load or other testable criteria.
Power, instrument air, fuel, software, actuation, operator actions, support structure.
Task ID, test method, calibration, inspection, frequency, evidence and failure escalation.
Technical Authority, associated MAH/bow-tie, drawings, codes, deviation/MOC links.

blocks.t: Set criteria in quantities or evidence that inspectors and technicians can check: valve stroke and seat performance, pressure relief set point, fail-safe response, gas-detector response, integrity of passive protection, structural remaining capacity and evacuation equipment availability. Qualitative claims such as “operates correctly” do not meet the standard unless a referenced test procedure defines an objective pass/fail method.
Verification procedures shall be traceable to individual PS requirements, record actual results and calibration/inspection limitations, and distinguish completed work from a demonstrated pass.

sections.title: 3.3 Technical ownership, change control and review

blocks.t: Discipline Technical Authority: Approves the PS technical basis, changes, verification criteria and risk-based exceptions within delegated authority.
Process Safety Lead: Challenges MAH barrier adequacy, independence and link to risk studies.
Maintenance & Integrity Manager: Schedules and executes assurance tasks from the PS, reports any failure against criteria.

The PS is revisited after material process changes, repeat failures, damage mechanism changes, code updates, major accidents, integrity reassessments and life-extension decisions. Revisions are controlled through MOC and the ACE document-publishing workflow.

Routine first-line assurance is performed by trained operators, maintenance and inspection teams. Second-line technical reviews by the relevant TA check quality and outcomes. Independent or third-line verification is selected on the basis of risk, licensing obligations, criticality and evidence of systematic deficiencies; one verifier must not silently approve its own unchallenged nonconforming work.

rows: Closes on specified demand and meets approved stroke/seat test criteria within the required system response.
Partial/full stroke tests, cause-and-effect verification, leakage checks and bypass audit.
Opens within specified tolerances for the certified duty and discharge route; remains unobstructed and serviceable.
Set-pressure certification, inspection, blockage checks, maintenance history.
Detects defined hazard, votes/alarms/trips according to approved cause-and-effect, survives required environment.
Calibration, end-to-end tests, alarm response tests and fault monitoring.
Maintains design load capacity against degradation and fatigue assumptions.
Close visual/NDT surveys, corrosion/fatigue assessments, repair verification.

blocks.t: The values required in a particular PS are engineering approvals for that asset. This standard defines the content and accountability and does not invent universal stroke times, SIL targets or structural limits.

sections.title: 4 Integrity through the asset life cycle

blocks.t: At feasibility and concept selection, establish hazards, site conditions, regulatory constraints, lifetime, design codes, critical loads, corrosion exposure, materials, accessibility for inspection, reliability targets, decommissioning assumptions and uncertainty. Long-life risks such as inadequate inspection access, obsolescence, missing baseline thickness or unavailable spare parts should be addressed before the design becomes difficult to change.

Projects shall establish a documented design and integrity basis that defines intended life, operating conditions, applicable codes, critical risk controls, inspection/maintenance philosophy and technical authority approvals.

Design deliverables include controlled process drawings, calculations, equipment design datasheets, materials selection, hazard studies, weld procedures, inspection and test plans, functional logic and reliability requirements. Contractor quality plans contain mandatory hold and witness points, release authority and traceable certification. Vendor design deviations are treated as technical decisions, not purchasing concessions.

rows: Approved standards register, design basis, relevant studies, SCE list and preliminary performance standards.
Technical specifications, material traceability, critical vendor quality criteria, applicable codes.
ITP, weld/NDT and material records, pressure tests, electrical/instrumentation verification, punch-list control.
Equipment tags, test certificates, protected systems, as-built documentation and defects list.
PSSR, SCE test baseline, CMMS schedules, spares, operator competence and final acceptance records.

blocks.t: An asset or major modification shall not be accepted into routine service without an authorised handover dossier, critical barrier evidence, controlled operating limits, approved procedures, maintenance and inspection plans, and Area Authority release.

The receiving Operations and Maintenance functions accept the equipment and technical data, not only the physical handover. Open punch items must be categorised and risk-assessed; critical defects prevent operational acceptance. Starting operation does not close project obligations to deliver as-built information.

During operations, field evidence is compared with the original duty and remaining-life basis. Fatigue, changing production chemistry, higher water cut, pressure cycling, corrosion allowance consumption, obsolescence and deferred maintenance may invalidate design assumptions. The programme updates inspection intervals and risk controls when that occurs. MOC is required for changes to barriers, limits, maintenance strategy or technical basis.

Technical Authorities shall consider ageing and obsolescence where remaining design life or performance margins may no longer be adequate; continued operation beyond the demonstrated integrity basis requires a documented assessment and approval.

Life extension decisions take account of actual condition, original design basis, deterioration, defect history, fatigue and corrosion estimates, barrier redundancy, operating duty, inspection access, spares, emergency response and uncertainty. Decommissioning plans address residual hydrocarbons, wells, pipelines, contaminated material, isolation, structural stability and temporary work risks.

Life extension or retirement dossiers shall identify assumptions, independent review where warranted, technical authority endorsement, residual risk decision, work plans, and asset records transferred or archived under ACE-DOC-STD-001.

Asset integrity activities are selected on the basis of applicable laws and codes, credible degradation mechanisms, criticality, baseline condition, risk studies, service history, SCE performance standards and inspection effectiveness. Statutory requirements and mandatory minimum frequencies take precedence over convenience or production availability. The responsible TA approves risk-based adjustments to intervals when supported by sound evidence.

Every critical asset and SCE shall be assigned appropriate inspection, testing, calibration and maintenance tasks in the controlled CMMS or approved inspection system, including due dates, acceptance criteria, competence and evidence requirements.

The asset register links functional location, equipment tag, serial number, parent process system, drawing, installed configuration, SCE classification, maintenance strategy and inspection circuit. Work orders and condition findings use the same identifiers. Duplicate aliases, orphaned tasks, missing equipment locations and untraceable test reports are data-quality nonconformances.

The Maintenance & Integrity Manager shall reconcile changes made by MOC, capital projects and equipment replacement into the equipment hierarchy before routine work planning is transferred to Operations.

Risk-based inspection evaluates susceptibility to damage, probability of failure, consequence and the effectiveness of proposed inspection methods. For pressure systems and piping, define corrosion loops, damage mechanisms, inspection locations, wall thickness and limits; for rotating equipment, define vibration/oil/electrical monitoring; for structural systems, define corrosion, fatigue, foundation and connection checks. Critical assumptions and uncertainties are recorded and challenged.

rows: Internal/external corrosion, erosion, cracking, fatigue, overpressure.
Inspection plans, measured thickness, NDT, remaining-life review, repairs.
Bearing failure, seal loss, misalignment, vibration and lubrication.
Condition trends, overhaul, seal performance and root-cause actions.
Sensor drift, logic faults, demand failure, bypass or obsolescence.
Calibration, end-to-end tests, diagnostics and proof-test findings.
Corrosion, fatigue, vessel impact, foundation damage, dropped objects.
Structural inspections, fatigue assessments and defect repairs.
Pressure loss, corrosion, leakage, external damage, annulus anomalies.
Barrier tests, corrosion/integrity surveys, monitoring and well/pipeline programmes.

blocks.t: The Materials & Corrosion Lead maintains damage-mechanism reviews for asset systems exposed to produced fluids, seawater, atmospheric exposure, chemicals and variable operation. The programme establishes chemical treatment, corrosion monitoring, coatings, cathodic protection where appropriate, inspection circuits, environmental limits and monitoring frequency. The effectiveness of control is verified by data rather than assumed from injection volumes alone.

When process chemistry, fluid composition, operating temperature or protective treatment changes materially, the corrosion-control basis and associated inspection programme shall be reviewed through MOC.

sections.title: 5.5 Maintenance execution, test quality and feedback

blocks.t: Work packs include permit and isolation requirements, competent discipline, job steps, calibration standards, original and as-left readings, acceptance criteria, quality hold points and reinstatement actions. Failed tests are defect records even when adjustment subsequently produces an acceptable result; recurring failures are assessed for systemic causes.

The work-order record shall retain equipment ID, task version, execution date, technician, supervisor acceptance, actual findings, measured values, failed criteria, corrective work, deferral reference and as-left condition.

Safety-critical inspection, maintenance and proof-testing shall be completed by its approved due date or deferred only by an authorised risk-based decision endorsed by the relevant TA and linked to any required deviation.

Prioritise due tasks by risk, barrier importance and shared system dependencies. The monthly backlog review identifies overdue unapproved work, duration beyond due, repeat deferrals, insufficient access and resource bottlenecks. Where maintenance is impossible at safe operation, the asset owner considers shutdown or restriction rather than automatic administrative extension.

Turnaround and offshore campaign scopes combine statutory inspections, inaccessible equipment, safety-system tests, major repairs, spare availability and opportunities for verification. The project schedule records critical-path inspection hold points and reinspection criteria; evidence is entered into the asset history before return to service.

Contract inspection and NDT providers are selected based on competence, procedure approval, equipment calibration, reporting quality and independence appropriate to the risk. The accepting ACE TA remains accountable for the technical disposition of findings.

An anomaly is any departure from an approved design, performance criterion, operating limit or expected condition, including failed proof tests, corrosion beyond prediction, structural defects, leaks, unacceptable instrument performance, missing integrity evidence or recurring alarm faults. The first action is to determine whether a critical barrier or operating limit is currently affected.

A discovered defect shall be recorded against a uniquely identified asset or SCE, screened for immediate risk, and escalated to the Area Authority and relevant TA where it may impair a barrier or create an unsafe condition.

rows: Loss of containment, unavailable SCE, unknown immediate stability or possible Very High risk.
Secure or stop affected operation; urgent TA and Area Authority review; deviation if applicable.
Degradation with credible progression, lower performance margin or High/Medium risk.
Record interim restrictions, approved remediation date and monitoring.
Demonstrated tolerable degradation with no compromised mandatory criteria.
Include in maintenance/inspection plan with evidence-based review date.

blocks.t: The above classes guide workflow urgency but do not replace ACE Risk Matrix risk ratings or acceptance authorities. If uncertainty prevents credible safety verification, treat the condition as potentially impaired pending a competent assessment.

sections.title: 6.2 Fitness for service and remaining-life assessment

blocks.t: When defect severity exceeds routine maintenance disposition, conduct a documented engineering assessment using an applicable code or recognised method suited to the damage mechanism. Establish actual dimensions and uncertainties, loading, operating range, degradation trend, remaining life, fracture/fatigue significance and inspection confidence. Define the scope and limits of continued operation, not merely a pass/fail conclusion without conditions.

Any decision to continue operating with a defect that compromises an SCE requirement or mandatory standard must have TA-endorsed technical basis, correct corporate risk acceptance, an approved deviation where required, and Area Authority verification of the stated conditions.

Corrective work defines permanent repair criteria, approved methods, materials and inspection/test hold points. Temporary repairs are treated as controlled changes or deviations as appropriate, with expiry, operational constraints and final-repair plan. Repair execution does not close the anomaly until inspection or testing verifies that the required function has been restored.
Defects and anomalies shall remain open until restoration is verified, the technical record is updated and the accepting authority has formally closed the associated work and risk records.

Repeat failures and common degradation are grouped by mechanism and contributing factors. Trend reviews consider poor design margins, material defects, installation practices, maintenance quality, operator workarounds, inspection coverage, system-wide corrosion exposure and obsolescence. Investigation outcomes lead to revised strategies, inspections, technical standards or hazard studies as appropriate.
Keep a controlled anomaly register with condition, evidence, risk category, remaining life, restrictions, repair priority, TA review, action status, close-out tests and links to incident/MOC records.

An SCE is impaired when it is unavailable, bypassed, degraded below an approved criterion or cannot be demonstrated to meet required performance. Examples include an inhibited fire and gas detector, ESD valve with failed seat test, overdue pressure-safety device assurance with no approved deferral, or lost emergency power redundancy.

A known or suspected SCE impairment shall be brought to the Area Authority immediately, risk-assessed, entered in the impairment register and managed under a controlled deviation before continued operation under restricted conditions is considered.
Personnel may stop work or secure plant immediately to protect safety. Unauthorised operation with an impaired barrier is not an acceptable temporary maintenance strategy.

Assessment addresses the major accident scenarios for which the barrier is credited, whether related safeguards share common causes, likely demand conditions, time to repair, compensating safeguards, human reliability and emergency-response degradation. Restrictions can include reduced throughput, isolation of a unit, limits on simultaneous work or full shutdown. The replacement safeguard must be feasible and independently monitorable.

rows: SCE ID, failed criterion, affected MAHs, status and discovery date.
Area Authority records stop/restrict/isolate decision and communication to shifts.
Risk Matrix current/residual levels, barrier independence and compensating protection.
TA endorsement, VP/CEO risk decision where applicable, deviation and expiry.
Repair, objective test to PS, removal of restrictions, final Area Authority release.

blocks.t: A deferral request identifies why required work cannot occur by its due date, exposure created by the delay, residual risk, alternate monitoring, limiting conditions, revised deadline and restoration owner. Technical endorsement is based on actual equipment condition and available evidence, not only resource constraints or production loss.
No safety-critical task shall be rescheduled beyond its authorised date without a recorded, risk-assessed deferral endorsed by the responsible TA and approved at the applicable risk acceptance level.

For deviations from mandatory technical or operating requirements, ACE-OMS-STD-002 applies in addition to this standard. Safety-system inhibits and overrides must comply with Control of Work and be controlled at the point of use: register location, scope, permit, time limits, protections and reinstatement verification. A long-standing inhibit is not deemed acceptable because it appears in an operations log.

Core targets: zero unapproved SCE impairments in service; zero unapproved overdue safety-critical tasks; all active deviations reviewed before expiry; all restored barriers functionally tested before status is changed to Available.

sections.title: 8 Structural, pipeline and well integrity interfaces
8.1 Offshore platform and marine structural integrity

blocks.t: For Pommerac A, Chenet B and Sapodilla C, establish the approved load and environmental basis, inspection zones and critical structural components, fatigue-sensitive details, impact exposure, marine growth, corrosion protection and access/egress dependencies. Analyse findings for their significance to local and global structural performance. The Offshore Operations Manager controls access and operational restrictions while Structural and Marine TAs decide technical acceptability.

sections.title: 8.2 Subsea pipelines, risers and land flowlines

blocks.t: The pipeline and flowline integrity programme defines routes, operating envelopes, fluids, design and corrosion limits, crossings, unsupported spans, third-party interference, mechanical damage, isolation capability and leak detection. Monitoring and inspection techniques reflect service conditions and credible threats, with explicit management of data gaps at buried or inaccessible sections.

Pipeline and flowline defects affecting containment or ability to isolate shall be assessed by the responsible Pipelines TA with Operations, Process Safety, Materials & Corrosion and Environmental interests as appropriate.

Well integrity is managed through the Well Integrity Management Standard and dedicated barrier records covering well design, installation, annulus pressure, mechanical barriers, well-control equipment, testing, interventions and abandonment. The Wells function retains primary accountability for well integrity while the shared ACE risk, MOC, deviation and document controls apply. Facility-to-well interfaces such as tree shutdown and surface ESD remain explicitly mapped to both systems.

sections.title: 8.4 CPF process containment, tank farm and jetty

blocks.t: At the CPF, the integrity basis includes separation, compression, gas conditioning, sales-gas metering to the Gas Buyer, crude stabilization, storage, loading and jetty transfer. Focused threats include pressure containment, corrosion/erosion, rotating seals, tank bottoms, bunding, custody transfer safety interfaces and marine loading isolation. Joint reviews with Operations and commercial interfaces ensure integrity constraints are not lost during nominations or transfer operations.

sections.title: 8.5 Interfaces to engineering standards and MOC

blocks.t: Technical Standards define the required engineering baseline; asset-specific performance standards and inspection plans interpret them for each plant configuration. Design changes and significant shifts in degradation rate must follow MOC. Engineering, Operations, Wells, Supply Chain and HSE share a change record so there is no gap between what was approved, installed, tested and operated.

Related technical documents: ACE-ENG-STD-901 Engineering Standards Framework and Technical Authority Standard; ACE-ENG-SPC-410 Safety Instrumented Systems Specification; ACE-WEL-STD-001 Well Integrity Management Standard; ACE-AIM-STD-002 Inspection Management Standard; ACE-MOC-PRC-001 Management of Change Procedure.

blocks.t: Use leading indicators (task compliance, overdue critical actions, unapproved deferrals, failed barrier tests, inspection coverage and data quality) alongside lagging results (loss of containment, serious equipment failure and repair backlog). No percentage KPI is interpreted without its numerator, denominator, exceptions and confidence in underlying asset data.

blocks.t: Area Authorities and Maintenance & Integrity perform monthly reviews of SCE health, overdue assurance, active impairments and significant anomalies. The Integrity Engineer consolidates cross-asset trends and reports quarterly to the VP Engineering & Projects and the TLC. Technical Excellence maintains a register of material overdue risks, new technical standards and systemic lessons. A formal annual programme review includes maturity, capacity, competence, resource constraints and priority interventions.
VP Engineering & Projects: Chairs quarterly integrity performance review and ensures technical and financial capacity for risk reduction and necessary asset decisions.
Area Authority: Owns the integrity status communicated at shift and operating meetings and executes appropriate operating restrictions.
Integrity Engineer: Maintains the consolidated portfolio dashboard and evidence of assigned improvements.

sections.title: 9.4 Escalation, audit findings and corrective actions

blocks.t: Significant integrity breaches, unapproved barrier impairments, recurrence of major defects and missed mandatory inspection requirements shall be escalated to the relevant VP and the independent assurance function, with actions tracked to verified closure.

Audit findings are classified and prioritised using the established ONE risk and action systems. Closure verifies the operating effectiveness of a changed control rather than merely the publication of a revised procedure. Findings with potential systemic relevance are shared with other ACE assets and related discipline owners.

sections.title: B.2 Worked example: Pommerac A ESD valve

blocks.t: An ESD valve on Pommerac A may be credited as a containment and isolation barrier. The PS states the approved initiating signals, required isolation duty, fail-state, allowable closure response and test acceptance, pressure/differential conditions, actuator dependencies and required survivability. Evidence comprises full/partial stroke records as applicable, seat checks, end-to-end logic verification and maintenance actions. An unsuccessful test immediately triggers anomaly and impairment screening; successful retest does not erase the failure history.

sections.title: B.3 Worked example: CPF fire and gas function

blocks.t: A CPF gas-detection function is defined by hazard coverage, detector suitability, location, alarm/logic response and protective action. The PS identifies calibration and end-to-end functional testing, inhibited-device visibility, power and logic dependencies, and post-maintenance reinstatement. A detector bypass is not a routine work order; it is managed as an impairment with Area Authority decision and restoration verification.

1. Detect, document and preserve evidence, including failed test results and operating conditions.

sections.title: Appendix G — ACE operating scenarios and integrity decisions
G.1 Gulf of Paria platform integrity issue

blocks.t: During an offshore structural survey, a critical support on Pommerac A shows accelerated local corrosion. The report records measurements and the original acceptance criterion. The Structural TA evaluates load path, corrosion progression, possible temporary protection and inspection confidence. The Offshore Installation Manager restricts relevant loading or access until safe continued use is justified. The remaining-life basis, repair and verification are tracked as an anomaly, with MOC if the structural basis or configuration is changed.

sections.title: G.2 CPF relief valve testing failure

blocks.t: A CPF relief device fails a scheduled bench test. The equipment record retains the failed result; the Process/Mechanical TAs assess protection coverage, like-for-like replacement, overpressure scenarios and compensating measures. The Area Authority decides whether the protected unit remains in operation. The device is returned to Available only after a demonstrably acceptable function test and completed reinstatement checks, not merely because the maintenance work order was closed.

Trend data for a Pawpaw Lease flowline shows unexpectedly rapid thickness loss after a change in produced-fluid composition. The Materials & Corrosion Lead revisits the damage mechanism and control effectiveness, the Pipelines TA verifies remaining life, and Land Operations applies restrictions as indicated. Changed treatment, inspection intervals or equipment must follow MOC where the approved basis is altered.

sections.title: G.4 Offshore safety-system impairment during maintenance

blocks.t: A proof test on Pommerac A requires a controlled temporary inhibit of an ESD input. The work pack identifies actual loss of protection, alternate safeguards, permit and isolation, bypass register, time limit and post-test reinstatement. The Area Authority and relevant TA approve and verify controls at the required level. A longer-running inhibit is referred to the deviation process; the shift log alone is never adequate approval.

sections.title: Appendix I — Damage mechanisms and inspection effectiveness

blocks.t: Inspection strategies begin with the anticipated failure mechanisms, not a standard inspection calendar. Each equipment group is reviewed against design materials, operating environment, age, history, previous findings and expected progression. The Inspection Lead and affected TA record method capability, coverage and probability of detection, including known limitations. Where direct access is impractical, supplementary process and condition monitoring is applied but not represented as equivalent assurance without technical justification.

blocks.t: The review compares predicted deterioration with actual inspection findings: if failure rates, thickness loss or unusual damage increase despite nominal completion compliance, revise the inspection plan and challenge the underlying model. Record missed defects and detectability limitations as learning inputs; inspection is not “successful” merely because a planned job was completed.

Where the selected inspection technique or access cannot reliably demonstrate the required performance criterion, the responsible TA shall approve an alternative assessment, increased coverage, enhanced protection or restriction before claiming compliance.

blocks.t: For each critical protective function, identify sensors, logic, final elements, instrument air or electrical supply, communications, human intervention, bypass and maintenance provisions. Record whether the dependencies are themselves SCEs or support several credited barriers. The Technical Authority verifies that a failure at a single shared utility or controller has not been counted as multiple independent safeguards in an associated hazard study.

sections.title: J.2 Managing failed and incomplete SCE tests

blocks.t: Failed proof-test events are recorded at the instant failure is found. A successful repair and repeat test proves restoration, not that no failure occurred. If a test was partially executed, the missing portion is documented against the specific PS requirement and remains an exception until demonstrated. A rolling aggregate compliance rate must show both test completion and actual pass/fail performance.

sections.title: J.3 Deliberate impairment versus accidental impairment

blocks.t: Deliberate impairments arise during planned maintenance, bypass, calibration or testing and require pre-job controls and signed reinstatement. Accidental impairments arise from a fault, damage or failed verification and demand immediate operations triage. Both are entered in the same control register, but the evidence of approval and corrective work will differ. A permit can control the job without authorising continuing impairment of the barrier.
Impairment records shall identify initiating cause, affected MAH, discovery or start time, alternative controls, expiry, approval, normalisation checks, restoration test and final release.

sections.title: Appendix K — Risk-based inspection decision and technical endorsement

blocks.t: 1. Define pressure boundary or equipment system, asset ID and intended service, design specifications and the applicable inspection code or company standard.
2. List credible damage mechanisms for normal, transient, start-up, shutdown and foreseeable abnormal service; capture the evidence for each.
3. Identify potential failure modes, consequences and existing safeguards using the ACE risk matrix and relevant hazard assessments.
4. Review inspection history and confidence: age, prior measured condition, uncertainty, monitoring access, inspection coverage and detectability.
5. Select techniques, locations and intervals that can credibly demonstrate required integrity; ensure competence and data-quality requirements.
6. Define warning, action and rejection criteria, with a route from findings into anomaly management and risk reassessment.
7. Secure Inspection Lead and relevant Technical Authority endorsement; publish tasks and data sources in the controlled systems.

sections.title: K.3 Risk acceptance and technical endorsement

blocks.t: The Inspection Lead demonstrates the method, the TA endorses technical adequacy, the Area Authority decides whether the actual equipment can be operated within limits, and the appropriate risk authority accepts residual exposure under ACE-RSK-STD-001. These approvals are complementary. A corporate risk acceptance is not evidence that the chosen inspection technique is technically adequate.

The RBI/inspection basis record shall contain its revision and author, affected asset/equipment IDs, methods, damage mechanisms, risk assessment, interval and decision, technical endorsements, limitations and linked CMMS task IDs.

blocks.t: A final handover matrix identifies each required deliverable, the accepting functional owner, revision and repository location. Typical missing items are vendor data, approved P&IDs, SCE test evidence, material certification, updated maintenance tasks, spare-parts lists and unclosed punch findings. Where a document is not required, the reason is recorded against the project scope; silence does not mean compliance.

sections.title: L.2 Legacy assets and incomplete data

blocks.t: Older ACE land and offshore assets may have incomplete original drawings or limited baseline inspection history. The integrity programme ranks those gaps by consequence, determines whether an interim operating restriction is needed, and creates a reconstruction plan using field survey, equipment examination and engineering verification. A legacy condition is not a standing exemption from the controlled technical baseline.

sections.title: Appendix M — Corrosion-loop and flowline assurance schedule

blocks.t: A loop groups equipment exposed to sufficiently similar fluids, temperatures, pressures, materials and damage mechanisms that a coherent monitoring and inspection strategy is technically justified. Loop boundaries are reviewed where flow, chemical dose, deposition, wet gas/liquid interface, water cut or pressure regime materially differs. The loop map links line numbers, equipment IDs, sampling points, inspection locations and corrosion-related incidents.

sections.title: M.2 Offshore line / land flowline response sequence

blocks.t: When changing production chemistry or unexpected loss-of-wall is detected, the Integrity Engineer and Materials & Corrosion Lead assess whether other components within the same loop share the threat. The Area Authority confirms operating conditions and necessary restrictions; the Pipelines TA assesses remaining containment capacity. Inspection scope is extended based on mechanism, not just proximity to the failed component. The learning is fed into MOC and strategy review for other affected assets.

For pipeline/flowline repair, retain original defect evidence, engineering acceptance, isolation and containment controls, approved repair design, work/inspection records, testing, as-built change, pressure/operating restrictions, corrosion plan revision and restoration approval.

sections.title: Appendix N — Equipment reliability and recurring failure investigation

blocks.t: Reliability programmes support integrity by reducing failure opportunities and controlling latent defects. Failure trends are analysed for their effect on major accident hazards as well as production impact. Repeated repairs to the same seal, valve, shutdown component or pump should trigger a mechanism investigation rather than continuing work-order turnover with no change in underlying condition.

rows: What precise duty failed, under which operating conditions, for how long, and how was it discovered?
Was the item specified for actual pressure, fluid, duty, environment and expected loads?
Were tasks suited to failure mechanism? Were prior defect patterns visible but ignored?
Was work access, competence, tooling, procedure or supervision inadequate?
Did start-stop cycling, product chemistry, capacity increase or frequent bypass create stress?
Were vendor data, CMMS records, MOC approvals, spare quality or project handover incomplete?
What measure eliminates/reduces recurrence and how will independent verification show success?

sections.title: N.1 Bad actor screening and action selection

blocks.t: A “bad actor” list is generated from repeat functional failures, high accumulated downtime, recurrent leaks, condition-monitoring trends and failure-to-close anomalies. Rank actions by actual safety and integrity risk, not exclusively by financial loss. The nominated owner considers design correction, operating regime change, material upgrade, revised inspection and maintenance, spares qualification and competence interventions.

After an engineering improvement, monitor performance for the period relevant to the failure mechanism. If corrective actions consisted of training or procedural changes, assess whether field work changed. Track repeat failures after “closure” as potential evidence that the investigation failed to reach the controlling cause.

sections.title: O.1 Pommerac A and normally unmanned wellhead platforms

blocks.t: Pommerac A has crew rotation, accommodation, hydrocarbon separation and offshore evacuation duties. Assurance plans must account for offshore work windows, instrument and safety function testing, logistical constraints, marine weather and critical spares. Chenet B and Sapodilla C require a deliberate remote-inspection and visit strategy: an unmanned status does not eliminate loss-of-containment, lightning, corrosion, isolation or emergency response hazards. Survey scope and equipment condition data are reviewed before visit planning and changes to isolation or communications.

sections.title: O.2 Central Processing Facility and jetty

blocks.t: CPF integrity priorities include pressure containment, compression, gas treatment, sales gas quality and metering, crude stabilisation, tanks, custody transfer and jetty operations. Interfaces between process safeguards, loading arrangements, marine vessels and the Gas Buyer gas transfer must appear in the AIMP. Tank inspection, bunding, loading arm or hose integrity and emergency isolation require coordinated scheduling to ensure work on one system does not remove another credited protection.

sections.title: O.3 Tamarind, Pawpaw and Soursop land leases

blocks.t: Mature land wells and gathering stations can experience variable fluids, corrosion/erosion, repeated repairs, uncertain legacy drawings and third-party interference. The Land Operations Manager and TAs rank inspections by credible release consequence, inventory and ability to respond. Flowline integrity is reviewed with mechanical condition, tank/gathering safeguards, field surveillance and maintenance support. An isolated small leak is assessed for systemic implications on parallel systems.

sections.title: O.4 Point Lisas Shore Base and contracted assets

blocks.t: At the shore base, cargo handling, lifting appliances, stored chemicals, marine transfer equipment, electrical infrastructure and contracted packages require documented fitness, certificates, inspection and maintenance controls. ACE-owned critical spares are preserved, tagged and protected so material condition is not lost during storage or transport. The Logistics & Materials Manager, relevant TAs and quality personnel maintain clear acceptance and rejection routes for spare and replacement materials.

sections.title: Appendix P — Technical Leadership Council assurance model

blocks.t: The TLC sets cross-company technical direction and ensures local operations and projects do not create incompatible engineering decisions. Its annual plan challenges at least one safety-critical function and one active degradation threat from each major asset grouping, samples critical deferrals and deviations, and evaluates whether design and field evidence support the published health status.
