docs.subtitle: Work authorization and coordination of hazardous activities at ACE facilities.

blocks.t: Purpose: define the authorization, coordination, field monitoring, suspension and closure of hazardous work. Applies to employees and contractors at CPF, offshore facilities, land operations and supporting sites where formal work authorization is required.

A permit confirms that scope, location, hazards, safeguards, isolation, personnel and validity have been reviewed. It is not a substitute for a risk assessment, isolation certificate, competence, or field verification. Work stops if conditions or scope change.

Parent: ACE-COW-STD-001 Control of Work Standard. Isolation is controlled by ACE-COW-PRC-002 Isolation and Reinstatement Procedure. The cross-functional flow is modelled in ACE-COW-PRS-001 Permit to Work Process (planned).
Stop the job if the scope, the conditions or the work party change. Do not continue on the existing permit.

Formal permit requirements follow ACE Control of Work Standard and site risk rules. Activities include hot work, intrusive process work, electrical work, confined-space entry, excavation, work at height, lifting, radiography, marine/diving work and hazardous maintenance. Additional permits may be required by site rules.

Permit type and supplemental certificates are selected by hazard and task. Routine work may use a simplified authorization only where ACE-COW-STD-001 explicitly permits it and risk controls remain equivalent.

rows: Gas testing, fire watch, fire protection, ignition control
Atmospheric test, attendant, rescue plan, entry log
Isolation, proving dead, earthing and competent personnel
Utility location, boundaries, shoring and inspection
Fall prevention, equipment checks and rescue plan
Lift plan, exclusion zone, appointed roles and equipment certification
Radiation controls, exclusion zone and notifications
Marine coordination, vessel/crew controls and operational interface

blocks.t: Work shall not be subdivided or narrowly described to avoid the authorization level its hazards require.

Area Authority coordinates activities and area conditions. Permit Issuer reviews work scope, risk controls, isolation and certificates, verifies the worksite and issues the permit. Performing Authority accepts the permit, briefs the work party and maintains compliance. Isolating Authority applies and verifies isolation under ACE-COW-PRC-002. Gas Tester records atmospheric tests. HSE advises and assures but does not replace operational authorization.

Roles must be filled by competent, authorized personnel. Independence is maintained where required by the Standard or risk. Shift transfer, delegation, role relief and permit ownership are explicitly recorded and accepted.

rows: SIMOPS, area conflicts, priority and coordination / coordination record
Accept, brief, monitor work party / permit acceptance and toolbox record
Isolation, verification and release / certificate and register
Test and record atmosphere / gas-test record
Advice, field assurance, escalation / assurance record

blocks.t: The Area Authority shall keep an overview of every active permit in the area and shall resolve conflicts before a permit is issued.
A permit shall only be issued by an authorized Permit Issuer and accepted by an authorized Performing Authority, and both names shall be recorded on the permit (C-COW-003).

Work requester defines equipment/tag, location, scope, boundaries, exclusions, work party, timing, tools, materials and completion state. Scope must be precise and match field equipment. Planning reviews current drawings, operating state, history, risk assessment, method statement, competence, emergency controls and worksite access.

Work package readiness includes isolation needs, permit type, gas tests, environmental controls, simultaneous operations, equipment condition, communication, rescue, PPE, test tools and dependencies. Incomplete or conflicting preparation is returned for resolution before permit issue.

rows: Equipment and boundary confirmed against current drawing and field
Hazards, controls, residual risk and crew briefing defined
Nearby work and shared system conflicts assessed
Authorized role, training and supervision available
Tools, PPE, instruments and certification serviceable

blocks.t: The work scope and boundaries shall be specific to the equipment tag and confirmed against the current drawing and in the field before permit issue (C-COW-001).
The hazards and controls in the risk assessment shall be reviewed with the work party in a recorded toolbox talk before work starts (C-COW-002).

Permit Issuer and Performing Authority check actual worksite conditions before issue. Verify tag, boundary, access, isolation, atmospheric test where required, barriers, signage, fire protection, environmental measures, communications and permit attachments. Discrepancies are corrected before authorization.

Permit record captures issue time, expiry, task, location, equipment, roles, hazards, controls, attachments, test results and acceptance. Permit is available at worksite. Validity is limited to approved shift/time; extension requires review, field revalidation and reauthorization.

rows: Crew understands hazards, controls and stop-work triggers
Issuer and Performing Authority acceptance recorded

blocks.t: The permit shall not be issued until the isolation certificate and any required gas test are valid and attached (C-COW-004).

Only authorized work proceeds. Performing Authority maintains permit conditions, briefings, barriers, housekeeping, worksite control and contact with Area Authority. Monitoring frequency reflects risk and duration. Gas testing and monitoring follow specified frequency and trigger conditions.

Stop and suspend work for alarms, changed conditions, loss of controls, isolation concern, scope change, permit expiry, material work-party change or SIMOPS conflict. Re-start requires revalidation, risk review as needed and rebrief. Material scope changes require amendment or new permit.
The Performing Authority shall monitor permit conditions at the frequency stated on the permit and stop work when any stop-work trigger occurs (C-COW-006).

Area Authority maintains an overview of active permits, shared systems, lifting areas, hazardous zones, access, traffic and emergency routes. Review interactions such as hot work near hydrocarbons, simultaneous energization and maintenance, pressure testing, marine activity, construction and operations.

Conflicting work is sequenced, restricted or stopped. Decisions and controls are recorded and communicated. High-consequence SIMOPS require risk assessment and designated approval; permit priority cannot override barrier integrity.
The Area Authority shall assess simultaneous operations before issuing a permit that shares a system, area or emergency route with other active work (C-COW-005).

Suspension is required when conditions change or work cannot continue safely. The Performing Authority makes the site safe, accounts for personnel and records status. The Permit Issuer/Area Authority confirms conditions for restart. Incoming personnel review permit scope, progress, hazards, isolation, safeguards, tests, outstanding issues and validity; handover is accepted and recorded.

Permit extension is not automatic. Revalidate worksite conditions, controls, isolation, atmosphere tests, crew and SIMOPS before extending within site rules. Expired permits require fresh authorization.
Every permit suspension and shift handover shall be recorded and accepted by the incoming Performing Authority before work resumes (C-COW-007).

Performing Authority verifies task completion, tools/materials removed, personnel clear, housekeeping, guards and temporary safeguards restored or identified. Outstanding defects and temporary conditions are handed to Operations. Permit Issuer and Area Authority confirm completion and hand-back.

Isolation release follows PRC-002. Permit closure alone does not authorize equipment return to service. Required inspections, testing, readiness checks and operational release are completed by responsible roles. Record closure time, attachments, residual issues and acceptance.
A permit shall only be closed when the Permit Issuer and Area Authority have confirmed completion and hand-back, and equipment shall only return to service through ACE-COW-PRC-002 (C-COW-008).

Record permit scope, risk assessment, approvals, issuer/performing authority, certificates, isolation references, gas tests, SIMOPS decision, suspension, handover, completion and close-out. Retain under Document and Records Management requirements.

Assurance samples field conditions against permit, authorization quality, isolation verification, gas-test compliance, scope changes, hand-back and record completeness. Measures include permit completeness, field checks, suspensions, repeat findings, isolation errors and corrective action closure.
Permits, attachments, gas tests and hand-back records shall be retained for three years under ACE-DOC-STD-001.
The Permit to Work Coordinator shall sample at least ten closed permits per site each month for completeness and field compliance (C-COW-009).
Leading: permits passing field verification first time; monthly sample completed (target 100%). Lagging: permit non-conformances found in audit; incidents involving permitted work.

blocks.t: Procedure for planning, applying, securing, verifying, maintaining, removing and reinstating isolations before hazardous work. Applies to process, electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, thermal, gravity, stored and other energy at ACE facilities.

Isolation boundary and method are selected by energy source, pressure, temperature, contents, configuration, possible re-energization and consequence. Control-system indication or valve closure alone is not proof unless the approved method explicitly accepts it.

blocks.t: Parent: ACE-COW-STD-001 Control of Work Standard. This procedure is used with ACE-COW-PRC-001 Permit to Work Procedure; no permit for intrusive work is issued until the isolation in this procedure is verified.
Do not treat a closed valve, a control-system inhibit or a panel indication as proof of isolation. Verify the safe state.

Isolation Planner identifies sources and points and prepares plan. Isolating Authority applies, secures, verifies and records isolation. Area Authority coordinates affected operations and work permits. Performing Authority checks boundary and precautions before accepting work. Operations controls system state and restoration. Technical Authority advises/approves complex or nonstandard isolation.

Competence and authorization are verified. Independent verification is required where defined by risk or Standard. Responsibilities for application, verification and removal are recorded; personal locks are removed only by owner or controlled exceptional process.
The Isolating Authority shall apply, secure, verify and record every isolation point on the certificate.
The Technical Authority for the discipline shall approve any complex or non-standard isolation before it is applied.

Define equipment/tag, scope, work limits, permit, safe state and restoration state. Review P&IDs, single-lines, cause-and-effect, equipment data, drawings, procedures and previous isolation records; physically verify points and resolve drawing mismatch before approval.

Identify pressure, vacuum, process fluids, electrical feeds/backfeed, batteries/capacitors, rotation, gravity, spring, accumulator, pneumatic/hydraulic, heat, chemicals, trapped volume, shared header, auto-start and induced energy. Choose single valve, double block and bleed, positive isolation, physical break, blank/spade or other approved method based on risk and standard.

Normal, alternate, stored, induced and cross-connected energy
Tag, location, type, position, lock and sequence
Method, test point, result, tester and verifier
Personal locks, lockbox, tags and briefing
Clearance, check, removal order, energization and hand-back

blocks.t: Every energy source, including stored, induced and cross-connected energy, shall be identified on the isolation plan and the isolation points shall be verified in the field before approval (C-COW-010).

Positive isolation is used when required by Standard, risk, intrusive scope or technical criteria. Consider valve reliability, leakage, differential pressure, hazardous contents, access and failure modes. Double block and bleed needs independently effective closures, a safe bleed route, a secured bleed and a monitored condition.

Blinds, spades, spectacle blinds, spool removals and physical breaks are tracked with location, rating, orientation and restoration status. Electrical isolation includes correct supply identification, lockout, proving dead with approved tester, proving tester before and after, discharge, earthing where required and backfeed protection. Control-system inhibit is not electrical isolation.
The isolation method shall be selected from the hazard and the approved criteria in ACE-COW-STD-001, and positive isolation shall be used where those criteria require it (C-COW-011).

Certificate/register captures equipment ID, permit, boundary, energy sources, points, method, lock/tag identifiers, application time/person, verification method/results, independent check, status, validity, affected work, owner and restoration evidence. Link drawings and permits; maintain unique records.

Locks/tags are durable, traceable and physically identifiable. Blind/spade and temporary breaks are tracked and reconciled at handover and closeout. Status is promptly updated. Group isolation uses controlled lockbox arrangements and individual worker protection according to site rules.
Every isolation point shall be locked, tagged and recorded with a unique identifier on the certificate and the isolation register (C-COW-012).

Operations prepares system state through approved shutdown, depressurization, draining, purging, cooling or other measures. Isolating Authority applies the approved sequence, locks/tags and records actual point status; affected operations are notified.

Verify safe state using suitable physical or instrumented method: zero voltage/proving dead, pressure test or vent/drain, try-start where safe, movement check, bleed monitoring, blind inspection or other validated test. Record readings, instrument, method, time and verifier. Failure or unexpected energy means stop, reassess and do not release permit for work.
The safe state shall be verified by a suitable test, recorded with reading, instrument, time and verifier, before the permit is released for work (C-COW-013).

Each exposed worker applies personal protection per site rules. Group lockbox arrangement ensures system locks remain secured and each worker is protected by their personal lock. Lock/key custody, spare keys, transfer and removal are controlled.

Exceptional removal of an abandoned lock requires confirming owner absence and work status, contact attempts, risk assessment, designated approval and notification before owner returns. Record the removal and review why normal removal was not possible. Tags alone do not replace required physical isolation.
Each exposed worker shall apply a personal lock to the group lockbox, and an abandoned lock shall only be removed through the approved exceptional removal steps (C-COW-014).

sections.title: 8 Maintain isolation and respond to change

blocks.t: Isolation validity is limited to defined scope and time. Review status at shift handover, permit suspension, scope change, extended stoppage, modification or changed operating conditions. Monitor integrity, pressure, bleed, alarms, lock/tag condition, adjacent operations and work party.

Unexpected pressure rise, flow, voltage, movement, leakage, compromised lock/tag or boundary change triggers stop work, withdraw as necessary, notify and reverify. Work resumes only after isolation is restored, verified and permit reauthorized. Extensions require review, not silent carryover.
Isolation status shall be revalidated at every shift handover, permit suspension, scope change or change in operating conditions (C-COW-015).

Performing Authority confirms work complete, personnel/tools clear, guards and covers restored, temporary earths/jumpers managed and defects recorded. Before removal confirm permits clear, personal locks accounted for, inspection/function tests complete, blind/spade/spool register reconciled and restoration sequence approved.

Applicable readiness checks include leak test, electrical test, lubrication, alignment, calibration, SIS validation, commissioning or pre-start checks. Operations and discipline roles agree readiness. Removing an isolation does not alone authorize equipment operation.
Isolations shall only be removed after clearance is confirmed, personal locks are accounted for and the blind and spade register is reconciled (C-COW-016).

sections.title: 10 Removal, restoration and return to service

blocks.t: Isolating Authority removes isolation in approved sequence after clearance. Personal locks removed by owners or approved exception; group lockbox reconciled. Account for blinds, spades, spool pieces, leads, earths, jumpers, tags and safeguards.

Operations verifies equipment configuration, position, pressure/temperature, electrical state, alarms, bypasses and operational readiness. Communicate controlled energization/pressurization and protect personnel. Abnormal leak, current, vibration, alarm or trip requires safe-state action and technical assessment. Close records only after restoration and handback evidence is complete.
Operations shall verify configuration and readiness before equipment is energized or pressurized, and records shall only be closed when restoration evidence is complete (C-COW-017).

Multiple systems, high consequence energy, shared services, remote equipment, unusual boundary, nonstandard method or drawing uncertainty require risk assessment, cross-discipline review and designated technical approval. Emergency actions may protect life or prevent escalation but must be recorded and followed by a separately planned and verified work isolation.

If required isolation cannot be achieved, work stops. Alternative safeguards require documented technical basis, risk review and approval under deviation/exemption controls. Do not assume compensating safeguards are equivalent.
If the required isolation cannot be achieved, work shall stop, and any alternative safeguard shall be approved as a deviation under ACE-OMS-STD-002 (C-COW-018).

Record plans, certificates, marked drawings, lock/tag register, tests, independent checks, group/personal locks, shift transfer, suspensions, deviations, exceptional lock removal, clearance, reinstatement checklist, restoration and permit closure.

Assurance checks field isolation against certificate, verification evidence, lockbox reconciliation, reinstatement completeness and status. Measures include verification errors, lock/tag discrepancies, overdue active isolations, exceptional lock removal, restoration defects and repeat findings. Assign actions and verify closure.
The Maintenance Superintendent shall check field isolations against their certificates on a monthly sample at each site and record the result (C-COW-019).
Leading: isolations verified independently where required (target 100%); lock and tag discrepancies found in sampling. Lagging: isolation failures; unexpected energy releases.

docs.title: Control of Work Standard
docs.author: Adrian Rodriguez — Permit to Work Coordinator (Offshore)
docs.custodian: Adrian Rodriguez — Permit to Work Coordinator (Offshore)
docs.reviewers: Arjun Khan — Permit to Work Coordinator (CPF); Roger Ramkissoon — Offshore Installation Manager; Luis de Verteuil — Land Operations Manager; Kavita Ramoutar — HSE Adviser
docs.applies: All ACE operated offshore platforms, land leases, pipeline work sites, Central Processing Facility, Point Lisas Shore Base and ACE-controlled contractor work.
docs.subtitle: Common site control of work, permit to work, hazardous energy isolation, SIMOPS, contractor supervision and safe return to service.

blocks.t: The Control of Work (CoW) system brings work preparation, risk assessment, permit authorisation, isolations, worksite coordination, supervision, changes, handback and learning under one process. It ensures that work is carried out by competent people on the correct equipment, within known boundaries and with controls that remain effective throughout the activity.

A permit is a communication and control instrument, not an approval to accept risks beyond ACE authority or an alternative to a safe method. The ability to perform work depends on safe plant condition, barriers, access, competence, operational constraints and ongoing verification. The Area Authority retains accountability for the site while the Performing Authority controls execution within the authorised scope.
Work subject to Control of Work shall be identified, risk-assessed, authorised, coordinated and verified before it begins and whenever a material change arises during execution.

This standard applies to work at the CPF and loading jetty; Pommerac A, Chenet B and Sapodilla C; offshore and land pipelines; Tamarind, Pawpaw and Soursop leases; and the Point Lisas Shore Base. It applies equally to ACE staff, contractors and vendor representatives. Remote or unmanned installations require an appointed Area Authority, a controlled communications plan and emergency provision appropriate to the task.

Routine operational activities may be managed by approved standing procedures where they meet the exemption criteria in the Permit to Work Procedure; an exemption is not automatic because a task is frequently performed. Work involving hazardous energy, breaking containment, hot work, confined space, hazardous lifting, excavation or impaired protection is screened for a formal permit and independent controls.

ACE-OMS-MAN-001; ACE-RSK-STD-001 Risk Management; ACE-AIM-STD-001 Asset Integrity; ACE-MNT-STD-001 Maintenance Management; ACE-MOC-PRC-001 Management of Change; ACE-PSM-STD-001 Process Safety; ACE-EMR-STD-001 Emergency, Crisis and Business Continuity. Implementing procedures: ACE-COW-PRC-001 Permit to Work; ACE-COW-PRC-002 Isolation and Reinstatement.

sections.title: 1.3 Hierarchy of safeguards and safe work

blocks.t: Risk management starts by eliminating or reducing hazardous activity through design, timing, remote methods, safer materials and engineering controls. Administrative measures such as permits and toolbox talks support but do not replace isolation, containment protection, guarding and monitoring where these are required. Several layers may be necessary for major accident hazard interfaces.

A work party assesses hazards from its own activity and hazards imposed on it by nearby plant or other teams. The plan identifies who has authority to stop work, which safeguards must remain available, how the task is suspended safely and who authorises restart. Operational pressure or a signed permit does not negate an observed unsafe condition.

No task shall proceed on an impaired safety-critical barrier, uncontrolled energy source or unknown plant status without an authorised technical and risk disposition that explicitly permits the activity.

sections.title: 2 Control of Work roles and authority

rows: Accountable for plant/site status and coordination; releases work, verifies conflicts, suspends and restores permission.
Checks permit scope, risk controls, boundaries, conditions, validity and permit register before issue.
Leads work team; confirms understanding, competence, implementation, monitoring and handback.
Prepares and applies authorised energy isolation, independent verification and later reinstatement.
Controls resources, competence, field supervision, method compliance and quality acceptance.
Maintains live permit picture, interface review, daily permit meeting and documentation quality.
Endorses technical changes, inhibited safety functions, special engineering precautions and barriers.
Ensures contractor staff competence, instructions, equipment suitability and compliance with ACE interfaces.

blocks.t: At Pommerac A the Offshore Installation Manager acts as Area Authority. For unmanned platforms and associated pipelines, the Offshore Operations Manager appoints the responsible control arrangements. The Land Operations Manager controls lease activities; the CPF Plant Manager controls the processing facility and associated worksite. The Point Lisas Shore Base uses its designated local Area Authority under the operations delegation.

One individual may hold more than one role only where the work category and company approval rules explicitly permit it; mandatory independent checks remain independent. Role delegation is made before the work starts and recorded so that shift changes, marine movements or contractor handovers do not produce an authority gap.

The Area Authority shall retain final control of whether work is released, suspended and handed back at the site, without relieving the Technical Authority of technical endorsement duties or the Performing Authority of safe execution.

For complex energy isolations, proof tests, confined space entry and impairment of protective systems, an independent competent person verifies the required critical control. Independence means a genuine second check by another authorised person, not a second signature added without field verification.

In small land or offshore teams, any planned variation to the normal role separation is escalated and approved under the applicable procedure before mobilisation. If independence cannot be achieved, the work is postponed or a demonstrably equivalent approved control is established.

Safety-critical isolation verification, override approval and return-to-service releases shall be performed at the authority level prescribed by the approved isolation and barrier-control requirements; self-authorisation is prohibited where independent approval is mandatory.

The nominated CoW System Owner maintains an up-to-date role register for permit issuing, accepting, isolating, gas testing and other specialist authorisations. Site organisations verify the named personnel against it, including offshore rotations and short-term contractor appointments. The evidence includes training, experience, practical assessment, validity and any restrictions.

A valid permit role is specific to the scope and location; an otherwise qualified individual is not automatically authorised to issue permits at an unfamiliar asset. Changes of appointed authority are communicated at shift handover and updated in the permit system.
CoW authorisations, competency assessments, delegations and suspensions shall be maintained in approved personnel and permit records and linked to the current role register.

sections.title: 3 Work preparation and task risk assessment
3.1 Work request, site visit and method selection

blocks.t: The work originator defines the equipment, site, work method, expected condition and boundaries. A joint visit by the Performing Authority and responsible site representative identifies piping and electrical energy sources, confined spaces, atmosphere, product inventory, lifting routes, escapes, simultaneous tasks and personnel or marine movement. The planner then selects the approved permit class and the controls needed.

The work pack identifies current drawings, technical instruction, required tools and competence, access arrangements, spares, test acceptance, waste handling and reinstatement. The issuer compares the scope with approved maintenance instructions and MOC records to prevent work on a wrong line, test point or valve.

Work descriptions and risk assessments shall uniquely identify the equipment, physical boundaries, authorised task, normal and abnormal conditions and the safe state in which the work will be performed.

sections.title: 3.2 Task risk assessment (TRA) and toolbox discussion

blocks.t: The TRA uses a sequence of identifiable work steps, credible hazards, existing controls, additional measures, responsibility and residual risk. It considers line of fire, stored energy, pressure, hydrocarbons, electrical hazards, ignition, falls, dropped objects, lifting, weather, marine access, vehicle movements, fatigue and emergency response. High consequence scenarios are explicitly connected to available barriers.

The toolbox talk checks whether the whole team understands the task, permit conditions, job boundary, isolations, changed circumstances and stop-work triggers. Workers are invited to challenge assumptions; the record confirms participation but cannot replace physical verification. Significant changes result in reassessment and reauthorisation rather than simply an added note.

rows: Equipment ID, location, approved instruction, duty state, site boundary.
Task steps, nearby plant, work parties, environmental conditions, failure scenarios.
Elimination, engineered safeguards, isolations, monitoring, PPE and competent roles.
ACE Risk Matrix, remaining uncertainty, acceptance authority and restrictions.
Field walkdown, toolbox attendance, live isolations, permit conditions and emergency route.
Stop work, update TRA, coordinate SIMOPS, amend or reissue permit as required.

blocks.t: Check certified equipment and lifting gear, tools calibrated where required, gas-test arrangements, access routes, communications, rescue capability, standby attendance, lighting, extreme weather and safe evacuation. Access to normally unmanned platforms is conditional on support vessel arrangements and defined emergency extraction.

The PA confirms fitness for duty, appropriate competence and absence of conditions that could impair safe performance. Where work interfaces with a live process, the AA arranges production/maintenance communication and restricts access, alarms or nearby work as necessary.

A permit shall not be issued when mandatory preconditions are unknown, failed or unverifiable, including incomplete energy isolation, required gas testing, unavailable rescue provision or an unresolved conflicting activity.

sections.title: 4 Permit to Work system and permit lifecycle

blocks.t: The permitted categories and site-specific thresholds are defined by the Permit to Work Procedure. At minimum, screening differentiates work with ignition potential, energy isolation, entry into confined spaces, breaking containment, excavation, work at height, lifting operations, electrical intervention and work near live process systems. Multiple hazards can require more than one control annex; splitting a job into two permits cannot be used to avoid integrated assessment.

The permit identifies exactly what work is allowed and under which current conditions. References to the TRA, isolations, certificates, sketches and SIMOPS assessments are part of the permit package. The issuer confirms that documents refer to the correct location, equipment and revision.

Every permit shall identify a unique number, site, worksite, equipment, activity, permitted period, responsible issuer and performing authority, linked risk assessment, critical safeguards, required certificates and handback requirements.

rows: Define scope, equipment, risk and preferred schedule.
Verify site boundaries, equipment identification and interfaces.
Plan, apply, test and record hazardous energy isolation.
Check live permit display, nearby work, production and emergency systems.
Verify all conditions, explain restrictions and release work.
Brief workers, check site, sign acceptance and begin only when ready.
Verify field controls remain effective; suspend if conditions change.
Account for people, materials, isolations, test status and plant readiness.

blocks.t: The issuing discussion is two-way: the issuer reviews the method and hazards; the performing authority demonstrates understanding and readiness. Where electronic issue is used, system authentication and field checks are both required; a click by someone remote from the site is not evidence of a completed walkdown.

The central permit display remains current throughout the shift and is available to operations, maintenance, contractors and emergency response personnel. Permit changes, suspensions and closing are time-stamped. The approved issue is distinguishable from drafts or applications.

The permit validity and any maximum extension are set by the implementing site procedure; the issuing authority confirms plant conditions and workforce at each renewal. A change of shift, temporary suspension, weather event or major operational transition requires reassessment against current site hazards and isolation status.

Handover includes open permits, active isolations, temporary overrides, nearby tasks, incomplete tests, contractor interfaces and emergency restrictions. The incoming authority acknowledges the status and physically checks critical items where required. A permit cannot simply be handed to an unapproved replacement PA.
A permit that has expired, been suspended, or materially changed in scope or worksite conditions shall not be used for continuing work until the appropriate revalidation or new issue is completed.

A job is suspended when controls deteriorate, process conditions change, a conflict emerges, an emergency alarm occurs, the crew leaves the area, or the stated task cannot be executed safely. The PA makes the worksite safe; the issuer records the reason and controls for the suspended state.

At handback the PA confirms work completed or the safe incomplete status, tools removed, personnel accounted for and temporary arrangements identified. Isolation removal occurs only via the approved reinstatement procedure. The AA verifies tests and operating readiness before clearing the permit; the recorded close-out does not supersede engineering acceptance where required.

Permit close-out and return to service shall require reconciliation of isolations, temporary services, bypasses, remaining hazards, equipment tests, work-party clearance and acceptance by the Area Authority.

Isolation planning identifies every energy source and credible means of re-energisation: electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, pressure, gravity, thermal, chemical and stored process energy. The appropriate isolation arrangement is selected on the basis of hazard, system pressure, inventory, work type and required standard. Schematics identify upstream/downstream boundaries, common headers, drains, vents and possible backfeed.

Positive isolation, double block and bleed, lock-out/tag-out and instrumented isolation are not interchangeable. Where hydrocarbon containment is opened or energy consequences are severe, the applicable technical standard determines the required physical separation. Control-system commands or a closed valve indication do not in themselves demonstrate safe physical isolation.

Before hazardous work begins, the Isolating Authority shall isolate, secure against inadvertent operation, test for zero energy or safe state, document the results and obtain independent verification where required.

rows: Equipment and valve tags, sources, backfeeds, worksite limits and safe drain/vent points.
Unique devices and IDs; controlled key custody; responsible IA and team interface.
Approved method, pressure release, vent/drain management and atmospheric checks.
Correct circuit identification, lock-out, test-before-touch and approved test equipment.
Independent check where required, actual observation, date/time, named verifier.
Maintained register, inspection, risk status, accountable owner and controlled change.
Hold point, personnel clearance, joint check, controlled sequence and plant acceptance.

blocks.t: Where several tasks share a common isolation, the certificate identifies each dependent permit and the authority to remove the last hold. Release by one work party does not end the protection of another. Transfer of responsibility across shift or contractor change is formally recorded.

Isolation registers are reconciled with live permits and operating logs. Unexplained devices or unknown isolation status are treated as an unsafe condition until investigated. Isolation extension or long-term retention is reviewed for corrosion, valve passing, tampering and operational conflicts.

The PA declares personnel and tools clear and confirms mechanical/electrical completion. The IA verifies all linked permits have cleared the boundary, removes devices under the approved sequence and checks process and electrical conditions. Technical tests, alarms and protective functions are performed before the Area Authority releases operation.

Where full functional testing is impossible before start-up, the Technical Authority assesses the limitation and any interim controls. Work remains under a documented restriction and the deferred test is explicitly assigned. A successful pressure restoration is not, by itself, evidence that all protective interlocks or alarms function correctly.
Isolation records shall retain the originating permit, boundary, application and test results, independent verification, linked jobs, handovers and final restoration / acceptance signatures.

sections.title: 6 Overrides and inhibits of safety systems

blocks.t: Overrides, force commands, alarm inhibits, relay bypasses and temporary defeat of protective devices may impair credited safeguards. They are controlled as barrier impairments whenever their function or reliability is reduced. The process addresses software, hardware and procedural bypass arrangements, including unintentional impairments introduced during maintenance or testing.

The request identifies exact affected function, initiator, operational need, expected duration, hazard scenario, alternate means, verification and restoration owner. The TA confirms technical effects and any potential interactions with shutdown logic or a common-cause failure. The AA determines whether the affected plant may operate and what additional restrictions apply.

A protective-system inhibit or override shall not be applied without the required Area Authority authorisation, relevant Technical Authority technical review and an approved time-limited impairment record.

Only named authorised personnel apply or remove bypasses. Application is checked against the precise device and function, then logged in the site bypass register and active permit picture. The field team communicates affected alarms and response actions to the control room. Operators must not rely on an alarm or trip that the current bypass makes unavailable.

The impairment remains visible across shifts and during emergency response. Its expiry and compensating measures are checked at each handover. Restoration requires verification of normal configuration and successful functional testing to the required degree. A bypass that cannot be removed is escalated as a defect and potentially an MOC issue, not given an indefinite extension.

An inhibited protective function shall be restored and verified, or a currently authorised impairment shall remain in force with explicit restrictions, before the related plant is returned to unrestricted service.

SIMOPS exists where concurrent activities can affect one another’s safety barriers, access, atmosphere, energy boundaries, emergency routes or operational decision-making. It includes work at different physical positions on a common process system, nearby hot work and hydrocarbon transfer, marine vessel operations, lifting over occupied areas, contractor scaffolding and emergency response readiness.

The Area Authority conducts an integrated review using the live permit board, schedule, operating state and change notices. Controls may include sequencing, physical segregation, communication windows, stop-work triggers, process shutdown, common permit hold points or appointment of an overall coordinating supervisor.

rows: Ignition source and vapour or release exposure.
Restrict one activity; verify atmospheres and transfer state before release.
Pommerac A lifting / active process work
Dropped loads, escape interference and shared deck access.
Exclusion zones, crane communication and task sequencing.
Pressure, ESD dependencies, shared emergency systems.
Joint risk review and formal interface control with OIM.
Underground services, vehicle strike, access to lease.
Line location, traffic management and monitored excavation limits.
Shared isolation holds; no reinstatement until entry cleared.

blocks.t: Work with a credible adverse SIMOPS interface shall be coordinated and authorised by the Area Authority against one integrated risk picture; independent permits alone do not demonstrate acceptable simultaneous operation.

sections.title: 7.2 Shift, contractor, marine and worksite interfaces

blocks.t: The permit meeting covers operational changes, weather, vessel schedules, shutdown systems, wells activity, tanker loading, high-risk jobs and temporary impairments. The CoW Coordinator maintains the permit/activities picture and identifies competing demands on lifting resources, isolations and emergency response.

For visits to unmanned Gulf of Paria platforms, vessel master, offshore Area Authority and work team agree communication, personnel tracking, access limits and weather contingencies. For land leases, multiple work parties coordinate vehicle access, shared lines and operating wells with the Land Operations Manager. The same principle applies to suppliers and vendors arriving from the Shore Base.
Material SIMOPS decisions shall record the activity conflict, participating work parties, responsible coordinating authority, agreed controls, communication plan and release/stop conditions.

Events requiring a new interface assessment include process start or shutdown, changed hydrocarbon inventories, unexpected gas test results, abnormal weather, loss of lighting or power, emergency-system impairment, loss of communications, additional contractors and revised lifting plans. Changed activity timing may require reauthorising otherwise unchanged permits.

No supervisor may downgrade a new hazard to a minor note simply to preserve the programme. The risk is escalated under the ACE matrix to the relevant approval level and the method adjusted. Where safe working cannot be demonstrated, work is deferred or stopped.

Before mobilisation, the contract owner verifies scope, technical and HSE qualification, identified site responsibilities, risk assessment competence, induction and evidence of the contractor’s training. The bridging arrangement sets which ACE permits, isolations, incident reporting and emergency arrangements govern the work. A contractor’s internal permit system does not replace ACE site authority unless a formal interface agreement states the conditions and approvals.

During execution, the ACE contract representative and PA check worksite conditions, subcontractor controls, staffing and changes to personnel. Contractor supervision is proportionate to risk; specialist expertise does not remove the AA’s duty to coordinate site hazards.
Contractors shall comply with ACE Control of Work arrangements and shall not commence site work without verified authorisation, competence and applicable bridging requirements.

Permit Issuers, Isolating Authorities, gas testers, confined-space entrants, standby persons, electrical specialists, lifting roles and other designated personnel require documented competency. Assessment considers practical demonstration and local systems, not training attendance alone. Site leadership checks expiry and restrictions in the authorisation register.

The PA sizes supervision to complexity, spread of work, hazardous energies and crew experience. Where a competent supervisor must leave, tasks are paused or formally transferred. Visiting vendors cannot accept an ACE permit role simply because they know the equipment.

Line managers are responsible for personnel competence and supervision; the Area Authority verifies local site authorisations; the Performing Authority confirms the competence and understanding of each worker in the executing team.

Communication uses permit meetings, shift logs, radio protocols, handover discussions, exclusion signage and updated worksite displays. Critical instructions are confirmed back by the recipient when misunderstanding could cause an accident. Translation or communication aids are arranged for contractors where necessary.

A handover identifies job status, equipment boundaries, unresolved defects, isolation state, bypasses, gas testing validity, weather and emergency constraints. The outgoing and incoming roles explicitly agree whether work is authorised, suspended or awaiting additional checks; ambiguity means suspension until verified.

sections.title: 9 Stop work, emergency conditions and restarting

blocks.t: Every person has both the authority and the duty to stop or challenge work when they judge that conditions are unsafe or controls are ineffective. Stop work is applied immediately for uncontrolled hazardous energy, wrong equipment identification, unanticipated releases, failed gas testing, compromised barriers, uncontrolled lifting and unsafe simultaneous activities. It does not depend on the most senior person on site being present.

The worker informs the PA and AA, withdraws people to a safe state and preserves evidence. The AA organises assessment with the appropriate specialists and ensures nearby work parties are advised. Work is not restarted by pressure to recover schedule or by an informal verbal reassurance.

Following a stop-work event, the affected activity shall remain suspended until the hazard has been controlled, the risk assessment and permit are updated as required, and the Area Authority records a restart decision.

On alarms or incidents, the site emergency response plan takes precedence over routine work permits. The PA secures the activity where safe, accounts for personnel and follows the command arrangements. Emergency teams are told of hazardous substances, temporary isolations, high-pressure tests, suspended loads and inhibited protection.

After an emergency, permits are not automatically reactivated. The AA confirms normal or restricted plant state, emergency system availability, changing hazards and adequacy of controls; the Technical Authority reviews technical damage or barrier impairment. Work parties receive fresh authorisation before restart.
Stop-work and emergency-related permit records shall capture the trigger, immediate controls, affected work, reassessment, approvals, restart evidence and any incident-report reference.

Work is complete only when the physical scope and critical verification are complete, all temporary arrangements accounted for, work parties and equipment clear, isolations returned to the approved configuration, and the AA accepts the safe state. Incomplete work is explicitly handed back with hazard signage and controlled protection, not recorded as normal service.

If a temporary modification or residual impairment remains, the AA ensures the operational team understands restrictions and that the decision is documented in the deviation / impairment system. Return to service is coordinated with Operations, Maintenance and the Technical Authority as necessary.

Field verification checks what is actually present: equipment identity, personnel understanding, isolation devices, hazardous energy tests, permit display, atmospheric monitoring, work method and site conditions. An administrative permit audit checks timing, authorisations, linked documents, expired or suspended permits, handback and traceability. Both are required, because a complete form can mask an unsafe worksite.

Sampling is risk-based, with priority for work involving hydrocarbons, high energy, SCE impairment, confined spaces, lifting and remote operations. Failed or repeated observations trigger immediate control, corrective action and assessment of systemic issues such as inadequate supervision or a flawed form.
The CoW System Owner shall maintain a programme of worksite verification, permit-system review and corrective-action tracking proportionate to the site risk and volume of hazardous work.

rows: Sample permits meeting scope, risk, authorisation and handback requirements; count critical faults.
Sample worksite controls found implemented and effective; report high-risk exceptions.
Unexplained locks, wrong boundary, failed independent check and late reinstatement.
Events by trigger and quality of reassessment; encourage early challenge, not suppression.
Current and overdue inhibits, compensating measures, expiries and restoration evidence.
Authorised roles current, site-specific and assessed; missing or expired approvals.
Detected conflicts, near misses, late changes and action closure effectiveness.

blocks.t: A low rate of stop-work events is not in itself proof of good control; reporting climate and field assurance findings must be examined together. Performance indicators are reported by site, work type and contractor involvement and interpreted with exposure. Findings feed into training, scheduling, technical standards and approved document revisions.

Site leadership conducts a periodic review of significant field exceptions, common permit failures, overdue bypasses, incidents and cross-functional lessons. The VP Operations receives material risk escalations and resource issues. Document Control manages controlled publication; changes to permit categories, isolation standards, responsibilities or electronic workflows follow the approved review and change process.

The standard is reviewed at least once every three years or earlier following significant incident, legal change, asset change, barrier failure, new work method or assurance finding. The approved ONE portal remains a navigation layer to source documents, not an alternative authority for issuing permits.

blocks.t: This is a screening aid, not a substitute for the controlled site permit category rules or specialist technical standards.

blocks.t: Electronic permit systems shall retain their audit history and display current status without allowing a superseded or withdrawn permit to be mistaken for an active authorisation.

sections.title: Appendix D — Isolation planning and reinstatement checklist

blocks.t: Identify all hazardous energy sources, including common headers, backfeeds and stored energy.
Confirm approved isolation method for the actual work and product inventory.
Inspect and identify the correct field equipment against current drawings.
Apply locks/tags and verify zero energy / safe state using approved test methods.
Record any independent verification and all linked work-party protections.
Maintain isolation visibility through shift changes and scope changes.
Confirm people and equipment clear before reinstatement authorisation.
Remove devices in controlled sequence and reconcile the isolation register.
Verify operational and protective-system function, with technical witness if required.
Complete Area Authority acceptance and update the work / permit records.

rows: Could the work change the pressure, fluid or energy state for another party?
Does hot work overlap venting, loading, hydrocarbon release or hazardous area work?

sections.title: Appendix F — Worked ACE site situations
F.1 CPF hot work beside operating process units

blocks.t: A fabricator proposes welding support brackets near a CPF process boundary during crude handling. The walkdown identifies product inventory, potential vapour sources, isolation access and concurrent loading operations. The Area Authority and CoW Coordinator examine whether the work can be relocated, scheduled during a quiet window or requires positive process isolation and continuous monitoring.

Only after controls, gas testing, emergency arrangements and conflicting tasks are resolved is the permit released. A change in tanker loading status or detection-system availability triggers suspension and renewed site assessment.

sections.title: F.2 Pommerac A ESD function test and marine transfer

blocks.t: The test crew seeks temporary bypass of an ESD function during a maintenance campaign as supply vessels approach the platform. The Offshore Installation Manager coordinates marine work, platform inventory, personnel on deck and protective-system status. The Technical Authority determines the allowable test arrangement and compensating measures.

The bypass is registered, authorised, time-limited and visible to all shifts. The crew records as-found test results and independent verification of normal restoration before the protection system is declared serviceable. A failed retest is handled as a live barrier impairment, not a permit closure administrative issue.

sections.title: F.3 Land lease excavation and shared flowline

blocks.t: A contractor proposes trench excavation near a Pawpaw lease gathering line while field operations continue. The Land Operations Manager coordinates line identification, as-built drawings, underground service checks, vehicle routes, pressure state and contractor excavation controls. The work party verifies the line physically under the appropriate procedure; a drawing alone is not sufficient.

An unexpected buried pipe or uncertain line identity triggers stop work. Work resumes only after the site risk assessment, permit and method are corrected and the responsible Area Authority formally reauthorises the activity.

sections.title: F.4 Chenet B normally unmanned platform visit

blocks.t: A small vendor crew is sent to Chenet B for instrument maintenance. The Offshore Operations Manager confirms delegated Area Authority, vessel suitability, communications, personnel count, emergency extraction and return weather window. The permit includes task boundaries and the isolation arrangement, with handover both to the crew and the onshore control point.

Loss of reliable communications or deteriorating marine conditions is a defined stop/withdrawal trigger. If work cannot be safely completed, the crew secures the equipment and records the remaining isolated or impaired state for further planning.

sections.title: Appendix G — Worksite field verification checklist

blocks.t: Correct permit number, scope and location match the actual job.
The people on site understand the task and can explain current hazards.
Equipment tags, valves, isolations and work boundaries match the plan.
Gas-test records and monitoring remain valid for prevailing conditions.
Mandatory controls and competent standby/rescue arrangements are present.
Any suspended or conflicting permits have been addressed.
Safety-system bypasses and impairments are visible and authorised.
Conditions and limits are understood by the incoming shift or contractor.
Temporary equipment and tools will be accounted for before handback.
The final permit handback contains test and restart verification.

docs.title: Document and Records Management Policy
docs.owner: Marvin Williams — VP IT, Data & Knowledge
docs.author: Marissa Bobb — OMS Manager
docs.reviewers: Marvin Williams — VP IT, Data & Knowledge; Sharda Bissoon — VP Legal & Government Affairs (General Counsel); George Habib — VP HSE & Compliance; Sophia Hosany — VP Operations; Dev Jaggernauth — VP Engineering & Projects; Nicole Lange — Head of Internal Audit & Risk Assurance
docs.applies: All ACE activities, sites, employees and contractors
docs.subtitle: The company commitment to one authoritative source, effective documents and trustworthy records.

blocks.t: ACE operates through one management system. Decisions, instructions and evidence that support safe and effective operations depend on information that can be identified, trusted and retrieved. This Policy establishes the corporate commitment to managing documents and records as controlled business assets throughout their life cycle.

The aim is not to accumulate documents. It is to make the applicable requirement available at the point of work, preserve the evidence that work was performed, and connect each document to the organisation, business process and OMS expectations it supports.
All ACE functions shall manage controlled documents and company records through the approved document and records management framework.
Documents that direct work shall be valid, current, clear, authorised and available to the people expected to use them.

This Policy applies to ACE employees, secondees and contractors who author, review, approve, issue, use, administer or preserve ACE information. It covers Head Office, the Point Lisas Shore Base, Pommerac A, Chenet B, Sapodilla C, offshore pipelines, the Tamarind, Pawpaw and Soursop leases, the Central Processing Facility (CPF), drilling and well service activities, projects and joint-venture activities for which ACE acts as operator.

It applies to corporate and operational policies, management system manuals, standards, plans, procedures, work instructions, forms, registers, drawings and specifications; to records created through those documents; and to electronically generated evidence such as work orders, inspection histories, permits, training evidence and incident records.

Information supplied by contractors or joint-venture partners that ACE uses to meet an operational, regulatory or contractual obligation shall be identified, verified and controlled at the point of acceptance into ACE custody.

Personal working notes and transient collaboration drafts are not automatically controlled records. They become subject to this Policy when they document a decision, obligation, approval, significant technical basis, transaction, test or execution of a controlled process. Separate information security and privacy obligations remain applicable.
The approved controlled repository shall be the authoritative source for each current ACE controlled document and its issue history.
ONE publishes and connects approved Word source material. The published web view is a navigation and presentation layer; it does not create a second authority independent of the controlled source.
Draft, superseded and withdrawn documents shall be clearly distinguished from current approved issues and excluded from active operational instructions.

Printed copies, downloaded files and extracts are convenient working material, but are uncontrolled unless a specific documented controlled-copy arrangement exists. Work teams must be able to identify the current revision before starting an affected task.
Every controlled document shall have a nominated owner, responsible custodian, registered number, document type, revision, status, review cycle and authorised approval route.
The hierarchy, numbering, review intervals and approval authorities in Part D of the OMS Manual shall apply throughout ACE.

Ownership follows the subject matter and operational accountability. Document Control maintains the identification and publication mechanism, but does not assume the technical or operational accountability of the owner. The Technical Authority evaluates discipline-specific correctness; the Area Authority makes sure the approved instruction can be used safely at the location.
Controlled Word documents shall use the approved ACE template, standard heading levels, OMS tags, document properties and applicable semantic paragraph styles.

The structured document is both the readable work instruction and the source from which ONE assembles the OMS wheel, functional views, process navigation, role-oriented views and search. Content should identify the action, the responsible role, the control and the record rather than rely on ambiguous statements of intent.
The relevant IOGP expectation tags shall be embedded at the document title and at the section level appropriate to the subject, with no unsupported or invalid tags.

sections.title: 3.4 Access at the point of work

blocks.t: Current approved operating documents shall be accessible to authorised users at each location where the relevant work is performed, including offshore, onshore and contractor interfaces.

Location-specific arrangements address vessel connectivity, offshore communications interruptions, shared consoles, shift handover and hard-copy operational packs. Offline copies need positive identification, custody and a reconfirmation method when connectivity returns.
Document owners shall communicate material changes and, where necessary, verify understanding or competence before an affected change takes effect.
Records shall identify what occurred, when it occurred, the asset or activity concerned, the originating person or system, and the status of review or authorisation where applicable.

Records supporting statutory compliance, asset integrity, operational readiness, HSE controls, commercial transactions and corporate decisions shall be captured in an approved repository with a defined retention class.

Records may originate in the maintenance system, inspection system, personnel system, project environment or corporate repository. A single document store is not required for every record, but each approved record class needs an identified system of record, accountable owner and reliable retrieval route.
Retention periods shall meet or exceed the minimum periods in the OMS Manual, applicable legislation, licence conditions and contractual commitments, using the longest applicable period.
Records subject to investigation, litigation, an audit hold, a preservation direction or a regulatory inquiry shall not be destroyed until the hold is formally released.

Access rights, backup, restoration, change history and secure disposal must be appropriate to the record classification and operational significance. A correction should preserve the original evidence and disclose when and by whom the correction was made.
Approved repositories shall apply role-based access, managed identities, recoverable backups and auditable administrative access appropriate to the information class.

ACE maintains operational continuity arrangements for critical current procedures and records where loss of the repository or network could prevent safe operations. Highly restricted personal, medical, privileged or commercially sensitive information remains segregated according to the relevant governing controls.
Document owners shall respond to reported errors, conflicting instructions, obsolete references and user feedback according to the significance of the resulting risk.

The effectiveness of document and records management is judged by currency, retrieval, practical usability, compliance with the publishing gateway, retention performance and the ability to produce reliable evidence during assurance.

In line with our values Integrity in everything and One team, one way, every controlled document is reviewed on time so that people can trust that what they read is current. Policies, standards, practices, processes, procedures and plans are reviewed at least every three years, emergency plans every year, and work instructions, forms and registers at least every five years, and earlier after a relevant change or incident (ACE-DOC-STD-001 §7). The review dates drive the document currency timeline in ONE.
The following responsibilities operate within the ACE solid-line reporting structure. Technical Authority and Area Authority roles provide additional control across functional boundaries.

rows: Approves Level 1 policy and directs company-wide compliance.
VP IT, Data & Knowledge — Marvin Williams
Owns the DOC system, resources, repository services, standards and reporting.
Custodian of the registration scheme, document templates, publication controls and records catalogue.
Maintains alignment with IOGP 510, the OMS Manual and expectation mapping.
Register documents, validate metadata, manage authorised publication, supersession and preservation.
Supports authors in clear procedural language, section structure, styles and OMS tagging.
Accountable for technical content, applicability, review, user communication and corrective action.
Endorse discipline-specific technical requirements and changes within their delegated authority.
Make current documents accessible and applied at site; report discrepancies and document-use failures.
Interprets preservation duties, legal holds and legal/regulatory retention requirements.
Internal Audit & Risk Assurance — Nicole Lange
Independently tests compliance and the effectiveness of control arrangements.

blocks.t: System owner: The VP IT, Data & Knowledge is accountable for the design, ongoing effectiveness, resources and continuous improvement of the DOC system within ONE.
Document owner: The named owner is responsible for subject accuracy, cross-functional review, adoption, review dates and timely corrections.
Information Management Lead: The Information Management Lead is the gatekeeper for registration, metadata quality, the publishing route and controlled archival status.

No controlled document shall be marked Approved or made available for operational use until required reviews, Technical Authority endorsement where applicable, the specified approval and the publishing gateway have been completed and recorded.
Only Document Control shall assign or amend a controlled document identifier in the corporate register. Identifiers shall not be reused.

Draft revisions use letters A, B, C and subsequent letters; approved issues use 01, 02, 03 and subsequent numbers. A revision number is evidence of issue status only when the corporate register also confirms Approved.
An operational or engineering change shall trigger an assessment of affected documents, training, forms, drawings and records before implementation.
Conflicting instructions, failed retrieval, incorrect revision or missing safety-critical information are treated as operational-control defects, not merely formatting issues.

The accountable function resolves a technical conflict; the Information Management Lead ensures the approved resolution is reflected in the controlled information system. Until resolution, the Area Authority determines whether work may proceed within approved controls.
Approval evidence, superseded issues, revision histories, design and integrity evidence, audit reports and disposal certificates shall remain traceable to their source, custodian and retention class.
Destruction of any eligible record shall require an authorised disposal decision and verification that no active hold or longer retention requirement applies.
Any proposed departure from the established document and records controls shall be referred through the applicable OMS deviation process before implementation.

An administrative exception cannot waive a statutory preservation duty, the approval authority for a safety-critical instruction, or the requirement for a current approved source of operating instructions.

The DOC system owner reviews a quarterly dashboard and outstanding control weaknesses with the Information Management Lead and OMS Manager. High-consequence deficiencies are escalated immediately; periodic performance is reported through the wider ONE assurance and management review processes.

rows: Approved documents past scheduled review date / documents due for review. OMS Manual objective: below 5%.
Failed checks and approved exceptions by type and owning function; repeat error trend.
Verified cases and corrective actions, including site and contractor findings.
Audit sample of required evidence, metadata completeness and retrieval outcomes.
Records due for disposal, blocked by holds and authorised disposal evidence.

blocks.t: Material deficiencies identified through document-use incidents, conformance reviews or internal audit shall be recorded, assigned to an owner and tracked to verified closure.

The Controlled Document and Records Lifecycle Procedure describes the required operational steps. Detailed standard requirements are assigned to the Document and Records Management Standard and the Operational Document Publishing Standard. The OMS Manual remains the governing hierarchy and approval authority.
ACE-OMS-MAN-001, Revision 03 — One Management System Manual, Part A and Part D.
ACE-DOC-PRC-001 — Controlled Document and Records Lifecycle Procedure (associated implementing procedure; pending controlled issue).
ACE-DOC-STD-001 — Document and Records Management Standard (document programme priority; issue status to be checked in the register).
ACE-DOC-STD-002 — Operational Document Publishing Standard (document programme priority; issue status to be checked in the register).
ACE-OMS-STD-002 — Deviation and Exemption Standard (applicability to be verified when issued).

Where a technical standard, site work instruction or records schedule imposes a stricter control than this Policy, the stricter applicable requirement governs, subject to formal resolution of any direct conflict through the owner and approval authority.
Process owner of ACE-DOC-PRS-001: the Information Management Lead, as recorded in the Process Register (ACE-BPM-REG-001).

sections.title: 7.2 Standards and practices that implement this policy

rows: Controlled Document and Records Lifecycle Procedure (under ACE-DOC-STD-001)
Data Quality and Information Management Standard

blocks.t: The owner reviews this Policy at least every three years, or earlier after a major regulatory change, significant document control failure, material technology change or change to the ONE publication framework.

rows: A formally registered and approved instruction, policy, standard, plan, specification, form or comparable source with revision and ownership controls.
Retained evidence of a completed activity, decision, state, transaction, measurement, review or approval.
The approved controlled location from which a document or record is governed and retrieved.
The navigation, search and publishing presentation of authorised Word source material and approved metadata.
The accountable function or role responsible for content, applicability and review.
The designated, controlled application or repository that retains the authentic record.
A formal instruction to preserve defined records while a legal, regulatory or investigative need remains active.

docs.title: Controlled Document and Records Lifecycle Procedure
docs.owner: Marvin Williams — VP IT, Data & Knowledge
docs.author: Sanjay Jagessar — Information Management Lead
docs.reviewers: Ryan Ramsaran — Technical Writer / Procedures Specialist; Allison St. Hill — Document Controller; Paul Gomes — Document Controller; Marissa Bobb — OMS Manager; Sharda Bissoon — VP Legal & Government Affairs (General Counsel); Sophia Hosany — VP Operations
docs.applies: All ACE activities, sites, employees and contractors
docs.subtitle: Operating instructions for registration, authoring, verification, approval, publication, review, retention and withdrawal.

blocks.t: This Procedure describes the end-to-end work performed by document owners, authors, Technical Authorities, reviewers, approvers and Document Controllers. Its purpose is to ensure that staff use approved instructions, that changes are traceable and that business records remain reliable and available for the required period.

It covers controlled documents and records across ACE Head Office, the Point Lisas Shore Base, the Gulf of Paria platforms and pipelines, land leases, the Central Processing Facility, wells activity, projects and contractor interfaces. It applies to materials originally created in Word as well as received contractor or external documents accepted into ACE custody.
This Procedure shall be applied together with Part D of the OMS Manual. Where a more specific approved standard defines a greater requirement, the greater requirement shall govern.

The normal route creates one approved Word source, its registered metadata, a gateway evidence report, a publication event and communication evidence. For records, the route creates a captured record in an approved system of record, linked to its class, owner, retention and disposition rules.

Use the document-control workflow whenever a new requirement is introduced, an existing instruction needs revision, an MOC affects an instruction or drawing, a regulation or contract changes, a review comes due, a user reports an error, or a document is proposed for retirement. Use the records-control workflow at the point that a decision or completed activity generates evidence that must be retained.

rows: Function or system owner; approved business need
Initiate new controlled document and classify its type.
MOC owner; engineering or operations change package
Determine affected source documents, drawings, forms, records and user competence.

Verify continued validity, revise if needed or record no-change review.

Assess urgency and operating risk; open correction or restriction.
