Check acceptance criteria, asset applicability, custodian and record class.
Record class owner; retention schedule report
Verify hold status, audit or regulatory needs and disposition route.

sections.title: 3 Roles, authorities and segregation of duties

rows: States the business need, affected users, sites and process; supplies source evidence.
Accepts content responsibility, nominates author and reviewers, checks applicability and communicates revisions.
Creates accurate, implementable content, identifies requirements and records, and resolves review comments.
Supports structure, procedural clarity, template use, section mapping and semantic styles.
Document Controller — Allison St. Hill / Paul Gomes
Allocates document identifiers through the register; verifies metadata and issue evidence; publishes and archives.
Owns naming rules, register integrity, gateway exception decisions within delegated control, and publication assurance.
Reviews expectation mapping and alignment with the 10-element OMS framework.
Endorses technical requirements, technical deviations and affected safety-critical content.
Accepts the controlled content and the documented effect on their function or assigned authority.
Verifies that crews can retrieve and use current instructions; controls any local copies or restrictions.
Sets business retention class, determines hold applicability and authorises lawful disposition.
Samples the effectiveness and independence of the whole process.

blocks.t: Document Control shall not substitute its publication check for the technical, operational or managerial approval required by the OMS Manual.
The author shall not self-approve a document unless an expressly authorised, recorded exception within the approval framework permits that arrangement.

rows: Executive Leadership Team; Legal and element owners review.
Technical Authority review; Technical Leadership Council endorsement for technical Practices.
VP of the process owner’s function
Affected functions review; BPM system owner endorses cross-functional processes.
As required by governing technical content.

blocks.t: A document may involve multiple functions. Its one approving role is assigned by the class and ownership rules above; affected functions review and Technical Authorities endorse within their recognised jurisdiction. The approval record also states the version actually reviewed.

The following stages are performed in sequence. The record of each gate must be sufficient to reconstruct who decided what and against which revision. An incomplete or rejected gate returns the document to the named owner or author with an actionable reason.

rows: Approved request to draft, or written instruction to revise
Identifier, document class, registered owner and draft status
Structured Word source and required technical attachments
Comments, responses and consolidated review evidence
Decision made by the authorised approving role
Completed automated and human publication checks
Numbered Approved issue in repository; prior issue superseded
Communication and training or briefing evidence
Periodic review, change monitoring and controlled withdrawal

blocks.t: 1. Requestor records the objective, scope, process or asset, affected locations, expected users, initiating change or compliance driver, and the planned implementation date.

2. Document owner confirms whether an existing current document can be revised instead of creating a competing instruction. Search the ONE document map and register for overlaps or active supersession.

3. Select the document class and ownership under the OMS Manual hierarchy. Identify whether the material is corporate, technical or site-specific, and whether technical endorsement or legal review is required.
4. Identify other documents, drawings, forms, work instructions and roles affected. For an operating change, record the corresponding MOC reference and readiness dependency.
The initial request and classification decision shall be recorded with the document identifier or change package reference.

Avoid parallel procedures for the same task unless the differences in asset, activity and authority are deliberate and clear. Reuse a single corporate standard with site-specific implementing documents where this is more reliable.

sections.title: 4.2 Stage 2 — Register and assign an identifier

blocks.t: 1. Author or owner sends the document request to Document Control with type, owner, system code, proposed title and, where relevant, site code.

2. Document Controller checks for duplicates and records the next available identifier under ACE-AAA-TTT-NNN-SSS. Use the three-letter system code and the controlled type-code table in the OMS Manual.
3. Allocate the first working revision letter A and Draft status. Record the owner, custodian, named author, expected reviewers and next control checkpoint.
Only Document Control shall issue a new document number. A retired or withdrawn number shall not be assigned to a new document.
A document changing to a different system or type shall receive a new identifier and explicit supersession mapping, rather than silently reusing its former identifier.

For example, a site-specific emergency plan may use ACE-EMR-PLN-001-CPF; a corporate procedure normally has no site suffix. Engineering standards use the prescribed engineering discipline number blocks.

sections.title: 4.3 Stage 3 — Author in the ONE Word template

blocks.t: 1. Create the source document from the controlled ONE template for its class. Do not begin by editing a downloaded PDF or an uncontrolled old copy.
2. Populate the cover, document-control properties, subject and applicability, full approval route, revision history and the required framing sections: purpose, scope, definitions and references.

3. Write an executable process in clear role-based language. Separate mandatory requirements, responsibilities, approval gates, records, risk controls and actual procedural steps using their corresponding ODS paragraph styles.
4. Use Title and Heading 1, Heading 2 and Heading 3 only. Place the section numbers in heading text; use native Word tables, captions, pictures and editable cross-references as appropriate.
5. Give each heading a stable bookmark so that ONE can link directly to that section even when its position in the document changes.

6. Insert an OMS Tags content control beneath the document title and relevant headings. Use valid expectation numbers separated by commas, without E prefixes or duplicates, and ordered from most relevant first.
A heading-level OMS tag shall apply to that heading’s section. A child heading shall not inherit the parent’s tag as an explicit claim of its own coverage.

For example, an approval step may have OMS 7.2; the technical review section may independently carry OMS 6.4 and 7.2; the records section may carry OMS 1.7 and 9.5. Title tags indicate coverage for the overall document.
Do not apply requirement styling to background description, or hide mandatory instructions in ordinary prose. The semantic style forms part of the machine-readable operational meaning.

sections.title: 4.4 Stage 4 — Internal quality check and review

blocks.t: 1. Author checks that each requirement has a clear owner or implementing role, each approval gate has a named authority, and each record has a capture and retention route.
2. Technical Writer checks procedural order, consistent terminology, level of detail, numbering, referenced files, tables, semantic styles, bookmark uniqueness and tag syntax.
3. Owner selects reviewers representing actual affected functions, Area Authorities and users. Where required, include HSE, Legal, Information Management and the OMS Manager.
4. Issue the review copy as a lettered revision. Compile substantive comments in one review record with the reviewer, section, concern, response and disposition.
5. Resolve contested requirements with the accountable functional owner and Technical Authority rather than silently removing safety or regulatory constraints.
Review responses, disposition decisions and final source revision shall be retained as approval evidence associated with the document number.
1. Identify the applicable approval route from the class matrix in section 3.1; verify the recorded owner and delegated authority remain current.

2. Obtain technical endorsement for technical and safety-critical content, including design envelopes, asset integrity criteria, isolation requirements, competence restrictions and barriers where applicable.
3. Provide the final reviewed Word source, open actions, resolved-comment record, change impact summary and effective-date proposal to the authorised approver.
4. Record the approving role’s decision and date against the exact source revision and checksum or immutable repository version identifier.
The approved issue shall not be released before all mandatory endorsements and approvals have been recorded; verbal agreement is not a substitute for issue evidence.

A material change after an approval decision invalidates that decision for the changed section unless the approver explicitly signs off the resulting revision. Editorial corrections that do not change meaning may use the controlled editorial-change path where authorised.
1. Document Controller sends the final Word source through the automated ONE gateway. Record file name, identifier, proposed revision and check timestamp.
2. Validate the document identifier, uniqueness, class and revision against the document register; verify mandatory document properties and an approval record.
3. Validate title tags and section tags for acceptable syntax, validity against the IOGP expectation register, order, duplicates and mapping to the registered document.
4. Validate allowed heading levels, heading bookmarks, style use, and substantive mandatory obligations that have not been assigned the correct requirement style.
5. Validate links to referenced ACE documents and identify missing or withdrawn targets, unavailable attachments and unrecognised site codes.
6. Classify outcomes as Blocking, Review Required or Advisory; correct all blocking findings before controlled publication.

rows: Invalid document number; missing approval; duplicate/invalid OMS tag; missing core properties; unresolved mandatory-style failure.
Reject publication and return to owner/author for correction.
Unresolved link, untagged substantive section, unclear owner assignment, unusual document type usage.
Document Controller documents decision and obtains owner clarification.
Editorial consistency, presentation or accessibility improvements that do not change meaning.
Record for improvement or correct before release where practicable.

blocks.t: A document that fails the gateway shall not be published until failures are corrected or a Document Controller records an accepted exception in accordance with the OMS Manual.
A check report is not a technical approval. The gateway checks structure, traceability and publication readiness; the approving authority remains accountable for the content.
1. After approval and gateway clearance, Document Control assigns the next sequential numeric approved revision: first issue 01, then 02, 03 and so on.
2. Update status to Approved and record issue date, effective date, approval evidence, owner, review due date, audience, registered content checksum and publication path.
3. Place the approved Word source in the designated controlled repository and make the associated ONE views available from that source and its tags.
4. Verify access to the full document and to the mapped heading sections through the OMS wheel, relevant function, process and role navigation where such mappings exist.
5. Change the superseded revision status to Superseded, remove it from default active retrieval and retain it in the historical record with its effective period.
6. Notify the document owner that the release is completed, provide the controlled location, and reconcile any previously registered controlled copies.
The register, approved source, approval evidence, gateway report, publication log and superseded revision shall be retained as a traceable issue package.
Never use a draft, superseded, withdrawn or unverified local copy as the controlling instruction for a live operation.

sections.title: 4.8 Stage 8 — Communicate, brief and verify use

blocks.t: 1. Owner assesses the effect of the issue on operations, engineering, maintenance, wells, contractors, competence, permits, site packs and related work instructions.

2. Identify the affected groups by function, location and role. For Pommerac A, include both offshore rotations and shore-based support; for CPF changes, include affected shift teams and contractor supervisors.

3. Communicate the change, effective date, affected document numbers and superseded instructions. Use targeted briefing and competence verification when changed control steps affect personnel safety or asset barriers.
4. Area Authorities or nominated supervisors verify that the current issue is retrievable at points of work and replace or withdraw registered local copies.
5. Where an approved document is a prerequisite for a changed operation, confirm readiness before the new work proceeds under the applicable MOC or commissioning process.
Briefing attendance, training acknowledgement, controlled-copy reconciliation and readiness decisions shall be retained when required by the change impact assessment.

sections.title: 4.9 Stage 9 — Periodic review, correction and revision

blocks.t: 1. Document Control provides review-due information to owners at an interval that leaves time for substantive review and authorisation before the expiry date.
2. Owner checks applicable law, organisation, asset configuration, process, technical standard, lessons learned, user feedback, references, roles and records requirements.
3. If content remains valid, retain a dated no-change review decision and reset the review due date under the governing cycle without misrepresenting the existing issue as a new revised text.
4. If content changes, initiate the revision using the current approved source, a draft letter and a documented change summary. Repeat affected technical, operational and approval gates.
5. If the document no longer applies, initiate controlled withdrawal and verify the effect on dependent documents and active work packs.

The review cycle shall be three years for policy, standards and procedures, annual for emergency plans and at least every five years for work instructions, forms and registers, unless a shorter applicable cycle is required.

Engineering standards and specifications also use a three-year cycle. An overdue review does not itself authorise a new instruction; the document owner must assess the risk and record a managed action.
1. Owner raises a withdrawal request stating the reason, replacement or successor if any, asset and location impact, dependent references and planned withdrawal date.
2. Document Control checks outstanding hyperlinks, ONE section mappings, active training resources, contractor work packs and controlled hard copies.
3. Obtain the owner’s authorisation and any required function or Technical Authority input, then mark the affected issue Withdrawn at the approved effective date.
4. Remove the withdrawn item from active operational navigation while maintaining a historical entry, reason, owner, revision and supersession trail.
5. Archive the content and associated approval history under the controlled retention rule; do not delete the identifier or recycle its number.
Withdrawal approval, notification and archive location shall be recorded in the document register.

sections.title: 4.11 Urgent safety corrections and temporary instructions

blocks.t: Urgent information may be needed before a revised full document can complete the normal review cycle. The owner and Area Authority jointly assess whether work should stop, remain restricted, or proceed only under an approved interim control. An urgent correction must not be achieved by circulating an uncontrolled replacement instruction.
1. Report the error or gap immediately to the Area Authority, accountable owner and Information Management Lead, including affected task, location and potential consequence.
2. Determine whether Stop Work, MOC, operating deviation, temporary procedure, site instruction or formal notice is required within the relevant governing standard.
3. Assign temporary document control, approver, scope, affected users, effective interval, expiry and withdrawal conditions before the interim instruction is used.
4. Communicate to affected shifts and contractors and retain evidence of acknowledgement. Track conversion to the permanent controlled revision.
No interim instruction shall bypass an applicable safety-critical approval, Technical Authority endorsement, Area Authority control or legal duty.
A short urgent work instruction is not a substitute for a full revision where the underlying process or barrier has materially changed.

sections.title: 5 Controlled copies, contractor documents and access

blocks.t: Some sites cannot assume continuous connectivity. Pommerac A, vessel operations, remote land leases and emergency teams may therefore maintain specially registered controlled sets for resilience, provided that they have a custodian and reconciliation process.
1. Area Authority requests an offline or hard-copy control arrangement and identifies the document set, custodian, location and verification frequency.
2. Document Control registers each controlled copy or signed offline package with its source revision and issued date.
3. Site custodian checks publication updates, replaces changed copies and records withdrawal of obsolete copies before affected work proceeds.
4. On restoration of connectivity, reconcile the local package and report any delay, discrepancy or use of outdated material as a document-control finding.
The controlled-copy register shall record copy ID, holder, location, source revision, date issued, last verified and date withdrawn.

Vendors supply equipment manuals, inspection certificates, drawings, test reports, commissioning records, as-built information and proprietary procedures. Their acceptance as ACE records does not automatically make every vendor instruction an ACE-controlled procedure.
1. Contract owner identifies contractual deliverables, document format, intended ACE use, information sensitivity and acceptance criteria before handover.
2. Technical Authority or nominated technical reviewer checks the content, completeness, revision and asset applicability of received technical deliverables.
3. The record-class owner determines whether the item is a reference record, technical baseline, approved supplier procedure or source material for an ACE-controlled instruction.
4. Document Control registers the received item and relationship to the ACE asset, contract, equipment tag, project and approved storage location.
A contractor procedure shall not displace an ACE-controlled operating requirement unless its use is formally accepted through the applicable contract bridging and approval process.
The system owner shall maintain access rights appropriate to the document or record classification, while ensuring that legitimate users can retrieve current operational requirements.

Read access to ordinary operational requirements is broad where possible; edit, approval, publication and disposal permissions are separated. Legal, personnel, medical, commercial and other restricted content is limited to authorised roles.
Changes to privileged access, ownership, major repository permissions and records-system configuration shall produce auditable evidence.

Records are generated by completing work, making decisions and verifying conditions. They differ from documents that instruct people on what to do. Some systems contain both: a permit template is a controlled document, whereas the completed permit is a record; an inspection plan is an instruction, whereas the signed inspection findings are records.
1. At process design or document revision, identify the expected records, their operational purpose, governing requirement, originator and required approval or review.
2. Assign each record class to a nominated owner and approved system of record; verify that it can be retrieved by asset, process, event, date or personnel identifier as required.
3. Specify minimum metadata and record quality conditions before personnel begin using the related form or system.
4. Verify that the record class appears in the retention register and is subject to the longest applicable requirement, including legal holds.

A business record shall be captured promptly after the underlying action, with sufficient context to establish what was done, who did it, the applicable asset or scope, the date and the applicable review or approval.

Examples include a signed permit and isolation certificate, CMMS work-order completion and test result, safety-critical element inspection outcome, shift handover, training assessment, well intervention report, contract approval and investigation action verification.
1. Originator creates the record using the approved system or controlled form and includes required identities, dates, references, asset or equipment tags, results and attachments.
2. Supervisor, verifier or approver checks completeness and plausibility where the process requires a second-person review.
3. Transfer or save the completed record in its system of record. Do not leave the only copy in a personal mailbox, chat exchange, removable drive or individual user folder.
4. Identify any correction transparently. Preserve the original state or available audit history and associate the correcting person, time and justification with the revised record.
A scanned signature page without its associated technical result, date, asset identity or full parent record may be inadequate evidence. Preserve the full evidential package and its context.

Different records use different databases and controlled repositories. ONE does not require extracting or duplicating every record into one store; it needs an approved catalogue of record classes and reliable links to the controlling application.
1. Record-class owner identifies mandatory indexing fields: record ID, associated document or activity, site or asset, record date, owner, classification and retention trigger.
2. Information Management verifies that stored items are retrievable through authorised pathways and that superseded technical baselines remain traceable.
3. System administrator confirms the required backup, restoration, integrity monitoring and access audit controls for the record’s risk and sensitivity.
4. For physical originals, record the custody location, responsible holder and check-in/check-out controls; include a scanned reference where this is authorised and useful.

The OMS Manual establishes the following minimum corporate periods. The Document and Records Management Standard will maintain the full approved schedule, including more specific legal, licence and business retention obligations. Retention may not begin until the correct trigger (for example project closure, asset retirement or employment termination) is known.

rows: Approved OMS documents and revision history
Design, as-built and asset integrity records
Life of the asset plus 10 years
Engineering and integrity record systems / Engineering owner
Permits to work and isolation certificates
Life of the asset plus 10 years

blocks.t: Where applicable law, contract, licence, investigation, safety case or other governing requirement demands longer preservation, the longer period shall prevail.

1. Legal & Government Affairs, Internal Audit, HSE or the accountable record owner identifies the records likely to be relevant to a threatened or active proceeding, investigation, audit or regulatory request.
2. Legal & Government Affairs defines the hold scope, start time, custodians and affected record systems and sends an instruction to the relevant record-class owners and system administrators.
3. Information Management and affected system owners apply retention locks or equivalent preservation controls, suspend routine disposition, and log acknowledgement from custodians.
4. Legal & Government Affairs reviews the hold periodically and authorises the documented release when appropriate; record-class owners then resume the ordinary retention assessment.
Preservation notices, acknowledgements, affected record scope, release decisions and system control evidence shall be retained in the approved restricted repository.

sections.title: 6.6 Archive and dispose of eligible records

blocks.t: 1. Records owner produces an eligible-for-disposition list from approved retention rules and verified retention triggers. Remove records still needed for ongoing operations, contractual claims or active assets.
2. Check active holds, pending inquiries, legal and regulatory needs, contract conditions and historical preservation requirements. Obtain Legal confirmation where applicable.
3. Obtain an authorised disposal decision from the accountable record-class owner and Information Management, in line with the approved retention schedule and delegated authority.
4. For permanent or extended-preservation records, transfer to the approved archival location with index, context, integrity protection and a retrieval owner.
5. For approved destruction, perform secure deletion or witnessed physical destruction as appropriate to classification, and record the method and completion date.
No destruction shall proceed without documented authorisation and confirmation that retention and preservation conditions are satisfied.
The disposal certificate shall include record classes, date range, source location, authorisation, hold check, destruction or archival method, operator and completion date.

Replacement of an engineering archive, enterprise content store, maintenance application or HR system must preserve evidence as well as the files. A technically successful migration is insufficient if revision history, signatures, assets, links or retention triggers are lost.
1. System owner inventories affected record classes, document identifiers, dependencies, preserved revisions and records under hold.
2. Define source-to-destination mappings for content, properties, authorship, history, access permissions and links; retain the source system as needed to establish fidelity.
3. Run sampled completeness, readability, checksum, access and retrieval tests with record owners before cutover approval.
4. Create a signed migration reconciliation report and controlled decommissioning decision. Archive source logs needed to explain subsequent record history.
Migration plans, test evidence, exception dispositions and acceptance decisions shall be retained as system-control records.

sections.title: 7.1 Error, obsolete information or publication failure

blocks.t: Any person may report a misleading procedure, wrong revision, broken ONE link, contradictory standard, missing safety-critical record or uncontrolled instruction. The response is proportional to the risk created by reliance on that information.
1. Capture the affected document or record identifier, location, user, current activity, observed failure and potential consequence.
2. Inform the document owner, Document Control and Area Authority where live operations could be affected. Apply Stop Work or task restriction where relevant.
3. Owner classifies severity and determines if MOC, incident reporting, technical deviation or urgent document correction is required.
4. Create an action record for correction, communication, evidence of removal of bad copies and verification that normal retrieval is restored.

A formal deviation from a substantive OMS requirement belongs in the governed deviation process; a limited technical publishing exception (for example a known converter limitation that does not change the approved instruction) can be decided within delegated Document Control authority if the gateway rules permit it.
A gateway exception shall identify the specific check, reason, affected section, risk, compensating control, decision owner and expiry or corrective-action requirement.
An administrative publication exception shall not permit missing approval, invalid operational authority, obsolete safety-critical instructions or breach of a legal retention obligation.

sections.title: 8.3 Monthly control checks and quarterly reporting

blocks.t: 1. Document Control checks overdue reviews, gateway failures, approved documents missing properties, inaccessible source files and unclosed replacement or withdrawal actions.
2. Record-class owners sample expected evidence for completeness, accessibility and age-appropriate retention; prioritise major accident hazard, well integrity, maintenance and permit records.
3. Information Management Lead consolidates exceptions by function, cause, operational consequence and trend, and proposes corrective action with owners and dates.
4. VP IT, Data & Knowledge reviews quarterly performance with the OMS Manager and reports recurring or high-consequence weaknesses through ACE assurance and management review.

The OMS Manual sets the controlled-document overdue-review performance objective below 5%. Other indicators should be baselined and assigned targets by the DOC system owner rather than presenting unapproved targets as existing corporate requirements.

sections.title: B.1 Pommerac A maintenance instruction change

blocks.t: A recurring ESD valve function test is changed because the equipment performance standard and maintenance task have been revised. The Maintenance & Integrity team identifies the work instruction, safety-critical element register, CMMS task, permit requirements and contractor briefing as affected items. The relevant Technical Authority endorses the technical change, the responsible manager approves the work instruction, and Document Control verifies metadata, tags and publication. The OIM ensures both offshore rotations receive the revised instruction before the next test. The old controlled copy is reconciled, and the approved test completion remains a maintenance record.

sections.title: B.2 CPF procedure correction discovered on shift

blocks.t: A CPF operator finds that an approved procedure cites the wrong isolation point after a plant modification. The operator reports the discrepancy and the Plant Manager assesses the immediate task under Stop Work and MOC arrangements. The owner initiates a corrected controlled issue, documents the affected technical basis and obtains the required reviews. A temporary instruction is only used if approved within the applicable authority. When the revision is issued, the shift teams are briefed and the outdated local copy is withdrawn.

A contractor delivers an ultrasonic thickness survey for a CPF vessel. The Inspection Lead verifies the report, asset identification, instrument traceability and findings. Document Control or the nominated record custodian registers the accepted report in the integrity records system under the asset. The retention class follows the asset-life-plus-ten-years minimum, subject to any longer relevant requirement or preservation hold. ONE may link the controlling inspection standard without duplicating the signed report itself.

docs.owner: Marvin Williams — VP IT, Data & Knowledge
docs.author: Sanjay Jagessar — Information Management Lead
docs.approver: Marvin Williams — VP IT, Data & Knowledge

docs.subtitle: Corporate controls for document ownership, identification, approval, repositories, retention and trustworthy records.

blocks.t: This Standard establishes the enterprise-wide controls by which ACE identifies, approves, issues, protects, locates, retains and disposes of controlled documents and records. A single controlled source supports consistent operations at Head Office, the Point Lisas Shore Base, the Central Processing Facility (CPF), the Gulf of Paria facilities, the land leases and project locations.

It governs documents used to direct work, demonstrate compliance, record technical decisions or provide operating evidence. It also governs records created by contractors when contracts require those records to become ACE property or part of an asset history. Technical adequacy remains the responsibility of the accountable subject-matter authority; document control establishes identity, status, accessibility and traceability.

Each ACE-controlled document shall have an assigned owner, unique identifier, document type, revision, status, approval authority, issue date, effective date, retention class where applicable, and a nominated authoritative repository.
An approved document shall be used for work only from the controlled source or a registered controlled copy managed under this Standard.
System owner: Accountable for the subject matter, application, cross-functional interfaces and periodic adequacy of their system documents.
Information Management Lead: Owns document nomenclature, master register, repository controls and confirmation that publication gates have been satisfied.
ACE-OMS-MAN-001, One Management System Manual, Part D — Documentation standard.
ACE-DOC-STD-002, Operational Document Publishing Standard — Word structure, OMS tags, semantic styles and gateway controls.

The hierarchy separates organisational policy, system rules, execution methods and task-level instructions. A document at a lower level implements, but does not overrule, a mandatory requirement from a higher-level document. The type code conveys the intended authority; it is not an indicator of document length.

rows: System owner on Executive Leadership Team
Function manager; Technical Authority endorsement when technical
As needed; at least every five years
Technical Authority, endorsed by Technical Leadership Council

blocks.t: A document shall be classified by the control decision it makes and the authority assigned to that decision; an author shall not reduce its level to avoid required review or approval.
Where a technical standard affects safety-critical equipment, the relevant Technical Authority shall review its relationship to the approved performance standards and engineering requirements.

The document owner decides whether content remains technically and operationally fit. The custodian manages the controlled object, its identity, lifecycle evidence and links. Authorship, custody, technical endorsement and approval may be held by different people; the separation is intentional.

The VP IT, Data & Knowledge owns this DOC system. Sanjay Jagessar acts as Information Management Lead and document-control gatekeeper. Allison St. Hill and Paul Gomes provide central document-control services; Sanjay Greenidge and Anil Ramdass support Engineering; Curtis Bobb supports Operations. The function maintains the central register even where a local controller manages the issue workflow.

rows: Capture, integrity, access and retention metadata

sections.title: 2.3 Ownership of cross-functional and site documents

blocks.t: Cross-functional documents have one accountable owner and named affected functions. For example, isolation requirements may originate with Operations but require review by Maintenance & Integrity and the relevant Technical Authority. A site-specific document includes a site suffix and an Area Authority who confirms it reflects the local plant configuration.

The Area Authority at Pommerac A is the Offshore Installation Manager; the Offshore Operations Manager covers the normally unmanned platforms and associated offshore pipelines; the Land Operations Manager covers the land leases; the CPF Plant Manager covers the processing facility. An Area Authority ensures site implementation; it does not replace technical endorsement or the document approval matrix.
Changes affecting more than one function shall be reviewed by each function with an accountable interface before issue.

ACE uses the identifier ACE-AAA-TTT-NNN-SSS. AAA is the system code approved in the OMS Manual; TTT denotes document type; NNN is the reserved sequence within system and type; SSS is a site suffix only where the document is site-specific. The controlled register records reservation, issue and eventual retirement without reusing any identifier.

blocks.t: Only Document Control shall issue a new identifier. Numbers shall not be recycled, including after a document has been superseded, withdrawn or cancelled.
A revision shall retain its existing number. If the system or document type changes, Document Control shall register a new document and link the earlier document as its predecessor.
1. The originating owner submits the proposed title, system, type, intended scope, site if applicable, proposed owner and justification to Document Control.
2. Document Control searches for duplicates or overlapping documents, confirms the classification and reserves the next available number.
3. The register records the reservation, the responsible owner, the expected approver, associated parent or predecessor, and a reservation status.
4. The author places the identifier in the Word cover, control table and properties, using the approved template. Document Control confirms consistency before review begins.
5. If the proposed document is abandoned, Document Control records cancellation and does not return the number to the pool.

blocks.t: Engineering documents use blocks 100 Process; 200 Mechanical and Piping; 300 Electrical; 400 Instrumentation and Safety Systems; 500 Structural, Civil and Pipelines; 600 Materials and Corrosion; 700 Wells and Subsurface; 800 Metering; and 900 General. The technical discipline code and owner are recorded in addition to the ENG document number.

A location suffix is part of the official identifier, not an informal filename suffix. A location-specific derivative of a company standard requires a clear delegation and explicit description of where company-wide rules still apply.
A site-specific document shall identify the site in its metadata and include an Area Authority implementation review.

The lifecycle begins with an identified operational, legal, technical or assurance need. The document owner confirms whether a new document is necessary or an existing document should be revised. Authors use the approved ACE template and apply the relevant OMS expectation tags, semantic styles and document properties described in ACE-DOC-STD-002.

Review is evidence-based. The reviewer examines accuracy against plant configuration, roles, prerequisites, required records, interfaces and implementation capacity. The author maintains a comment-disposition record for material comments, including why a technical objection was accepted or rejected. Reviewers do not approve by silence.
Document owners shall identify affected operations, technical disciplines, contractors and locations in the review plan before requesting approval.

Technical endorsement establishes that specialised technical requirements are acceptable; management approval establishes authority to issue the document within ACE. The publishing gateway checks the Word structure and minimum metadata, but automated acceptance does not mean the technical content has been independently verified.

The sequence is: review resolution; technical endorsement where required; formal approval; automated publishing check; Document Controller review of the gate result; registration and release. Evidence is linked to the exact Word revision that was assessed.
A document shall not move to Approved status or enter the current ONE collection without the complete approval matrix evidence and an accepted publishing-gateway result.

Issuing a controlled document has two actions: publishing the approved source and making the change effective for the operating audience. Document Control controls the first. The accountable line manager controls the second, including briefings, training and replacement of site copies. Publication alone is not proof that users can safely follow a changed task.

At Pommerac A, the Offshore Installation Manager confirms both rotating crews are briefed and the offshore controlled-copy register reflects the new issue. At the CPF, the Plant Manager coordinates shift coverage and affected maintenance interfaces. The Shore Base and land leases apply equivalent local checks.
The issue pack shall retain the signed decision, accepted Word source, gateway report, change summary, supersession link and notification evidence.

An urgent operational need does not suspend technical authority, risk assessment or approved work control. Where a temporary instruction is required, the accountable manager assesses the immediate risk, the relevant Technical Authority endorses technical limitations, and the authorised approver signs the temporary instruction under the appropriate governance. The instruction records validity, scope and expiry trigger.

An interim communication must not quietly become the permanent controlled procedure. The owner initiates the formal Word revision, records the temporary decision and reconciles affected instructions when the final document is issued.
A site team shall not rely on an unapproved draft to justify bypassing an isolation, safety-critical barrier, operating limit or permit requirement.

blocks.t: The first approved issue shall be revision 01; later approved issues shall use sequential numeric revisions. Draft letters shall not appear as approved operational issues.
The document register shall hold the complete state history, including the reason and authority for every change of status.

Changes are classified as editorial, administrative or substantive. Editorial changes correct grammar without changing a duty, limit or action; administrative changes affect title, owner or references; substantive changes affect control requirements, responsibilities, plant steps, technical content or required records. Each issued change receives a new numeric revision. The depth of re-review may be proportionate, but the approval matrix still applies.

Document owners review MOC outputs, incidents, audit findings, new legal requirements, plant changes, contractor lessons, technology changes and workforce feedback as possible revision triggers. A redline or comparison and a clear revision note are supplied for reviewers.

blocks.t: Supersession is a linked transition between approved revisions. Withdrawal removes the document from the current collection because the work no longer exists, the rule is consolidated elsewhere, or the document was issued in error. Withdrawal includes a business impact review and a communication plan; deleting a file is not a withdrawal.

A discovered publication error is logged as a nonconformance. Document Control can restrict visibility immediately when use presents a hazard, while the owner determines whether a formal revision, controlled correction or withdrawal is necessary. The prior approved source remains preserved for traceability.
A supersession or withdrawal record shall identify affected versions, successor if any, reasons, authorising role, communication evidence and disposition of registered copies.

sections.title: 6.1 System of record and separation of responsibilities

blocks.t: The approved Word document and its approvals remain the authoritative controlled document. ONE is the navigational and publishing layer: it reads the approved source to present expectation, function, process and role views, and links readers back to that source. The portal does not convert a rendered page or extracted section into a separately approved instruction.

ACE IT, Data & Knowledge administers access to the approved repository, version control, recovery and technical monitoring. Document Control decides which revision is current and maintains register integrity. System owners and function managers determine the appropriate readership and confidentiality.

Every Approved document shall have one identified authoritative Word source in the approved repository and one register record pointing to it. Copies or portal excerpts shall not acquire a separate official status.

Access is role-based and proportionate to sensitivity. Staff who perform work need reliable read access to applicable current procedures. Edit permission is restricted to controlled authorship and document-control workflows; a reviewer comment does not overwrite the official issue. Sensitive legal, personnel, security, health or commercial records are handled by their authorised owners and may be indexed without publishing their contents.

Electronic systems preserve timestamped revision and approval evidence. Backup, restoration tests, access changes and exception logs are managed under corporate IT controls. A retrieval path that depends on an individual employee account is not an acceptable system of record.
Where a cyber incident, broken link or repository outage makes the current instruction uncertain, the work owner shall verify an authorised controlled copy before work proceeds.

Offshore platforms, workboats, remote leases and restricted network zones may require approved local copies. Document Control maintains a controlled-copy register with holder, location, document ID, revision, issue date, update route and replacement acknowledgment. An uncontrolled printout is for reference only and may not be assumed current.

Contractors receive the specific controlled requirements required for their scope through the contract interface. A contractor repository or mobile application is not ACE’s master source; the responsible contract holder ensures the copy is current, records its distribution and retrieves obsolete copies when practicable.
The local controlled-copy register shall record withdrawal or reconciliation of prior issues after a new revision becomes effective.

Level 1 and Level 2 documents are reviewed at least every three years; Level 3 documents at least every three years except emergency plans, which are reviewed annually; and Level 4 documents as needed, not less often than every five years. Technical engineering standards and specifications are reviewed at least every three years. The register calculates and tracks due dates based on the governing interval.

A change in legislation, technical basis, major accident hazard, asset configuration, ownership, responsibilities, operating practice or known failure may require an earlier review. A review concludes with confirmation of continued fitness, a revision request, consolidation or withdrawal.
A document owner shall record a periodic-review decision even when no text changes. A review acknowledgment shall not silently change the approved issue date or revision.

The central register sends advance notice to owners and custodian teams. Overdue items are escalated through the relevant system owner, then to the OMS Manager and the executive owner if unresolved. Where the validity of a document is in question, the owner assesses whether operating use must be restricted pending review.

When an owner transfers or leaves ACE, the receiving manager nominates a successor and Document Control records the handover. Delegating authorship does not transfer executive accountability. Documents with no named owner are a control exception.
The periodic review log shall retain the reviewer, findings, decision, outstanding actions and resulting revision or no-change confirmation.

sections.title: 8.1 Document versus record and evidence integrity

blocks.t: A controlled document states what ACE requires or how work is to be performed; a record is evidence that an event, activity, decision, verification or result occurred. A blank permit or inspection form is a controlled document. Its completed, signed instance is a record. Both are governed, but they follow different lifecycle and retention rules.

Records originate in operational systems such as CMMS, integrity systems, permit systems, training records, investigation files, contracts and approved repositories. ONE may point to them or show their governing requirement; it must not replace their data authority without a controlled migration.
A record shall be attributable to its originator and activity, legible, retrievable, protected against unauthorised alteration and retained for its mandatory period.
Completed records shall be captured in approved repositories and shall not be held solely in personal drives, informal messaging or email inboxes.

The following corporate minimums reproduce the OMS Manual retention schedule. A law, licence, contract, litigation hold or regulator requirement may impose longer preservation; the longer requirement takes precedence. The retention trigger must be recorded explicitly where it depends on asset retirement or employment ending.

rows: Approved OMS documents and revision history
Design, as-built and integrity asset records
Permits to work and isolation certificates

blocks.t: Each record class has an owner, system of record, reference number, confidentiality level, retention rule and trigger, authorised access roles, preservation requirement and disposal authority. Activity-level metadata also captures asset or site, event or work-order reference, date of activity, originator, approver or verifier, and evidence of completeness.

An integrity record for a CPF pressure vessel includes the asset tag, inspection basis, findings, instruments and assessor; a Pommerac A valve function test includes equipment tag, test reference, acceptance result, deviations and signer. The record is registered against its physical asset to keep history intact after staff moves or contractors change.
Record stewards shall verify receipt, completeness and correct filing for records listed as mandatory deliverables in a contract, work pack, project handover or inspection plan.

The contract holder defines records to be delivered and their acceptance criteria before work begins. Project handover includes approved drawings, calculations, inspection certificates, as-built information, technical deviations, commissioning reports, equipment data and operation or maintenance data as applicable. The receiving technical owner checks fitness and indexes the records to the correct facility and asset.

A contractor transmittal alone is not evidence that ACE accepted the records. Deficient packages are returned with a punch list or managed under an approved turnover exception. The asset record steward owns subsequent custody.

Legal & Government Affairs may direct preservation of records relevant to a claim, investigation, regulatory request, contractual dispute or other formal hold. The hold is recorded by identifier, scope, owner, affected repositories and termination authority. IT and system custodians implement preservation and access restrictions; record owners suspend ordinary deletion for matching records.

Medical, personnel, security and commercially confidential records remain in their approved restricted systems with suitable access controls. ONE users see only the controlled requirements and metadata they are entitled to view.
No record subject to a legal or regulatory preservation hold shall be destroyed until Legal & Government Affairs has formally released that hold.

Archival follows supersession, withdrawal, completed operations, asset retirement or expiry of a working need. Archiving protects the evidence and removes confusion about current applicability; it does not itself authorise disposal. Retired approved documents remain linked in the register and can be retrieved for assurance, incident investigation or legal purposes.

Archive packages retain metadata, revision history, approval evidence and a stable identifier. File format conversion is controlled and validated against the source, with the original Word revision retained where required. Asset-life records remain accessible through asset retirement and the defined post-retirement period.
An archive manifest shall list the owner, location, date, record class, retention trigger, preservation controls and any hold or access restriction.

At the end of a retention period, the custodian proposes eligible records for disposal. The record owner verifies the class and trigger. Legal & Government Affairs checks holds and external preservation requirements. The Information Management Lead confirms the approved method and completeness of the evidence log. Destruction must be secure for the information classification and cover all governed copies where practicable.

Where a destruction request cannot be fully reconciled, the custodian records the unresolved locations and limits the decision accordingly. The disposal certificate is retained in the document/records register independently of the disposed content.
Disposition shall be authorised by the record owner and verified by Document Control, with Legal clearance where required, before physical or electronic destruction.

Approval, inventory, method, executor and completion retained

blocks.t: Document Control reports the health of the management system monthly to the VP IT, Data & Knowledge and the OMS Manager. Indicators are used to identify weak processes, not to reward rapid approval without substantive review. Measures distinguish source quality, gate quality, overdue review, site-copy accuracy and record retrieval.

sections.title: 10.2 Assurance, corrective action and executive oversight

blocks.t: The OMS Manager samples conformance to the framework; Internal Audit assesses design and operation of controls independently; system owners are responsible for first-line checks. Defects are classified by their potential impact: an incorrect safety-critical work instruction or missing approval takes priority over a minor metadata omission.

The Information Management Lead assigns corrective actions for publishing and repository weaknesses, monitors completion and keeps evidence of repeat verification. Persistent failures are escalated to the VP IT, Data & Knowledge and the applicable executive system owner.

If a current instruction cannot be shown to be approved and current at the point of use, the responsible Area Authority shall assess whether the activity can safely proceed under an alternative authorised control.

sections.title: Appendix A — Controlled document register: minimum fields

blocks.t: The register is an auditable index, not a substitute for the original Word file or for operational record systems. Fields are compulsory for current Approved documents unless the Information Management Lead records a non-applicable value and reason.

blocks.t: The corporate retention matrix states the minimum preservation duration; the operating record register identifies the trigger, repository and accountable steward. The examples below clarify the difference between a document that has a perpetual company history and an event record whose retention period begins only after a closing event. They do not shorten the minimums in the OMS Manual.

sections.title: E.1 Missing trigger data and preservation

blocks.t: When the asset retirement date, employment separation, final work closure or other retention trigger cannot be established, records remain preserved until the responsible owner reconstructs the timeline and Document Control verifies the basis. The register records uncertainty explicitly. An unidentified event date is not treated as the earliest possible date for disposal.
Record owners shall maintain the evidence supporting each retention trigger, including the event reference and the authoritative source of the trigger date.

sections.title: F.1 Offshore procedure change at Pommerac A

blocks.t: The Reliability & Maintenance Lead revises a work instruction for an ESD valve functional test. A Technical Authority reviews the updated test steps against the safety-critical performance standard. The responsible supervisor approves the new numeric revision, and Document Control registers the exact Word source after the gateway accepts its identifiers and tags. The Offshore Installation Manager checks the platform controlled-copy inventory, both operating rotations, crew briefing evidence and the CMMS work package reference. The superseded instruction remains in history but is removed from the current offshore copy set.

sections.title: F.2 CPF record receipt from an inspection contractor

blocks.t: The CPF receives an ultrasonic thickness survey from an approved inspection contractor. The Inspection Lead checks asset tags, measurement locations, equipment traceability, report completeness and technical acceptability. The record steward captures the signed report in the integrity repository and links it to the vessel. If the report indicates an anomaly requiring assessment, that action enters the integrity workflow. The report retention is based on asset life rather than contract end. A procurement close-out transmittal does not replace technical acceptance or the actual report in the asset history.

A migration may establish metadata and bookmarks, but it may not silently confer Approved status on historical draft content.
