blocks.t: A deferral shall be rejected where the proposed temporary safeguards do not reduce risk to an authorised tolerable level, or where the affected barrier cannot demonstrate minimum required performance.

The live barrier-status record identifies the impairment, initiating event, SCE or protection function, location, effect, assessed risk, compensating measures, approval, expiry, responsible person and recovery plan. The Area Authority verifies the controls on every relevant handover. Where production or work scope depends on the impaired barrier, limits are communicated to affected teams.

A temporary override initiated for testing remains a controlled safety-system bypass until verified removed. Temporary work-around instructions are not accepted as permanent operating philosophy; persistent or repeated impairment triggers technical review and MOC.
Barrier impairments and deferrals shall be retained with the equipment history, the deviation record, shift log, relevant permits and proof of final restoration.

Spares criticality reflects failure consequence, probability, repair duration, lead time, interchangeability, shelf life and access limitations. Items needed to restore or preserve an SCE are evaluated explicitly; a low-cost component may be a high-consequence stock item. Local stock level does not justify ignoring long supplier lead time or transport disruption.

The Reliability & Maintenance Lead and Materials function maintain a common critical-spares list. Offshore requirements account for vessel scheduling and weather; CPF requirements account for high-duty rotating equipment and process continuity. Substitutes require documented technical verification, including materials, ratings, firmware and certification.
Safety-critical replacement components shall be accepted against the applicable specification, traceable to equipment and preserved under suitable conditions; unapproved substitution is prohibited.

Point Lisas Shore Base receives, stores and dispatches maintenance materials, with road distribution to land leases and CPF. Receiving checks verify purchase order, manufacturer, part number, quantity, condition, certification where relevant, preservation requirements and shelf-life limits. Nonconforming goods are quarantined pending disposition.

Issue transactions associate parts to work orders or controlled reserves, preserving batch/serial trace where needed. Returned parts are labelled with service history and inspection disposition; unverified returns are not returned directly to serviceable stock.

rows: Cleanliness, packaging, temperature/humidity controls, shelf life and handling.
Model/firmware compatibility, calibration and approved technical equivalence.
Pressure/material rating, certificates, traceability and preservation.
Environment class, moisture control, certification and anti-static protection.
Periodic condition inspection, exercise where required, change monitoring.

blocks.t: The asset owner monitors end-of-support notices, scarce parts, proprietary software, discontinued components and supplier capability. The response may include lifetime buy, validated substitute, controlled repair or engineered replacement; permanent changes follow MOC and commissioning verification.

Spares forecasts are informed by failure history, operating duty, criticality, upcoming shutdowns and inventories across assets. Emergency purchases are traceable and subject to the same quality checks as routine purchase orders; bypassing receiving inspection is not an acceptable way to recover schedule.

Materials reliability review: critical spares availability, stockouts affecting SCE work, preservation nonconformances, emergency procurement frequency, unresolved obsolescence risks and quarantined safety-critical stock.

Shutdowns combine time-dependent inspection and maintenance, major corrective repairs, modifications, statutory obligations and commissioning activities. The turnaround manager integrates scope across Operations, Engineering, Wells, Supply Chain, HSE and contractors. The need for plant isolation and common utilities drives the schedule, not isolated work-order readiness.

The approved scope identifies critical path, outage assumptions, owner, resources, spares, crane or marine access, quality control and contingency for discovery work. All mandatory SCE and inspection tasks due within the outage window receive explicit disposition. Scope freeze controls require impact review for added or deferred work.

Before shutdown execution, the responsible Area Authority and turnaround lead shall confirm the outage basis, isolation plan, concurrent-operations constraints, emergency arrangements and readiness evidence.

rows: Inspection obligations, outstanding defects, risk and production window.
Detailed work list, resources, long-lead parts, cost and hazard review.
Maintenance & Integrity Manager accepts scope and readiness route.
Approved permits/isolations, execution plan, contingency and competent staffing.
Area Authority authorises outage work arrangements.
Hold points, tests, punch-list grading, document updates.
Engineering/maintenance certify work; TA accepts critical technical points.
PSSR, SCE status, operating limits, shift briefings and residual risks.
Area Authority releases operation; project owner closes records.

blocks.t: Restart readiness is evidence-led: all permits and isolations reconciled, critical bypasses removed or formally controlled, pressure systems tested, protective functions verified, quality dossiers accepted, operating procedures current and crews briefed. Open punch items are classified by consequence; critical unresolved items block the affected start-up.

The post-campaign review compares plan to actual, emergent defects, test failures, fatigue and working-hour risks, supply delays and lessons for future outage strategy. Any impact on equipment condition or operating duty is returned to the asset strategy and risk register.
The campaign close-out dossier shall retain approved scope changes, work-order links, test certificates, contractor handovers, residual defects, SCE status, PSSR sign-off and corrective actions.

Repeat failures, significant unplanned shutdowns, major maintenance-induced defects and failures of a credited barrier are investigated at a level proportionate to their consequence and recurrence. Analysis includes operational history, duty, alarm/trend data, component examination, common causes, environment, maintenance effectiveness, procedure adequacy, human factors and supply quality.

The investigation distinguishes physical failure mechanism, immediate event, management-system contributors and weak preventative barriers. Corrective actions address the cause and their effectiveness is independently verified. Replacing an identical failed component without reviewing the cause does not qualify as defect elimination.

Failures with potential major accident consequences or repeat SCE failure patterns shall be escalated to the relevant Technical Authority and HSE/Process Safety system for coordinated investigation and barrier review.

Reliability review tests whether the maintenance approach prevents the failure modes it was selected to address. Data may support changed task methods, intervals, monitoring limits, training, materials specifications or replacement designs. The change request states expected benefit, new risks, references and verification plan; changes to approved baseline use MOC.

Condition monitoring data should drive action before functional failure. Positive mean time between failures alone can mask short history or changing duty; failure counts, consequence and population exposure must be considered alongside the metric. High-availability assets deserve scrutiny of low-frequency high-consequence faults.
Reliability improvements shall have an owner, due date, technical endorsement where needed and evidence that the revised strategy or engineering control is effective after implementation.

Reliability findings at Pommerac A are screened for relevance to Chenet B and Sapodilla C, as well as similar equipment at CPF or land gathering stations. Common vendor models, firmware or maintenance practices may create fleet-wide exposure. Lessons are communicated through the maintenance network and, where suitable, formally issued as revised controlled procedures.

The reliability forum reviews persistent bad actors, barrier failures, deferred interventions and materials-related defects. Actions are tracked and closed with a demonstration that the deficiency has been corrected; a circulated alert without evidence of implementation is not an effective closure.

blocks.t: Targets are set through approved annual operating objectives; the table defines measures rather than inventing fixed threshold values. The reporting pack includes leading indicators (PM preparation, condition trends, defects under control) and lagging indicators (failures, downtime, barrier failures). Results require context such as throughput, duty, weather and planned shutdowns.

The Maintenance & Integrity Manager chairs monthly performance review with site operations, Reliability & Maintenance Lead, Technical Authorities and Materials. Exceptions include overdue SCE work, evidence gaps, deferrals, repeat failures, critical spares, data-quality defects and audit actions. Decisions are documented with owners and deadlines; failures of minimum barrier criteria are escalated at once rather than waiting for the meeting.

The VP Operations reviews serious recurring failures, material budget/resource constraints and corporate exposure. Technical standards and risk acceptance remain with the respective authorised roles. Audit findings are tracked to verification, and ONE can display links to relevant requirements without changing the underlying approved documents.

Monthly assurance records shall retain indicator definitions, data cut-off date, excluded records, evidence extracts, critical exceptions, risk decisions, assigned actions, escalation and subsequent verification.

sections.title: 10.3 Change control, competency and periodic assurance

blocks.t: Competence evidence for planners, technicians, supervisors and specialist contractors is maintained against role requirements, particularly for high-risk electrical works, pressure equipment, functional safety and lifting. Training completion alone is not proof of independent task competence. Spot checks sample both good and failed work orders, physical equipment status and the accuracy of CMMS records.

The standard is reviewed at least once in three years and earlier after major changes in legislation, company risk arrangements, new technologies, significant incidents or a material audit finding. The document owner proposes changes through the controlled ONE publishing workflow.

R = performs the work; A = single owner of outcome; consultees provide assurance or specialist review. Local delegation is documented and cannot override the approval matrix or Technical Authority rules.

sections.title: Appendix F — Practical ACE operating examples
F.1 Pommerac A emergency shutdown valve test

blocks.t: A planned ESD valve function test is coordinated with the Offshore Installation Manager and Control of Work coordinator. The work pack identifies the valve tag, hazard scenario, isolation requirements, approved proof-test criteria, instrument identification and return-to-service acceptance. The crew records as-found response and time, any failure, repair and independently verified retest.

If vessel access or operating constraints threaten the approved due date, the supervisor initiates the SCE deferral review before expiry. A production-driven schedule change does not constitute approval; the Area Authority and Technical Authority explicitly determine whether the affected operation can continue.

A trend increase in vibration on a duty compressor prompts diagnosis of loading, alignment, lubrication, bearings and possible common-cause effects on the standby unit. The Reliability Lead reviews condition evidence, risk, spares availability and a safe changeover window. The work pack specifies as-found vibration, acceptance after repair and any condition monitoring required before full duty.

If an engineered change to the seal or lubrication design is proposed, it is processed through MOC. If risk is beyond authorised tolerability, the Area Authority restricts operation while mitigation is arranged. The CMMS captures both the immediate repair and the root-cause action.

sections.title: F.3 Pawpaw lease pump and Point Lisas materials delay

blocks.t: A land pump shows repeated drive failures during seasonal access constraints. The planner checks the installed motor rating, drive history, equipment condition, exposure and spare logistics rather than issuing repeated identical replacements. Materials confirms compliant stock and lead time; the Land Operations Manager agrees an isolation and transport window.

If compliant spares are not available, a temporary substitution is not authorised by the storekeeper. The appropriate Technical Authority examines service fit and the change route, while the asset owner determines whether production restrictions or alternate methods are required.

sections.title: Appendix I — Assurance sampling and audit questions

blocks.t: Can the SCE register be reconciled to approved task versions and proof-test evidence?
Are all overdue SCE tasks visible with the correct barrier risk and approval status?
Do sample completed jobs include as-found and as-left results rather than only a close-out code?
Are maintenance strategy changes supported by engineering basis and formal MOC when required?
Do CMMS identifiers reconcile to field tags, drawings, warehouse items and asset history?
Does a sample of work packs show correct isolations, crew competence and return-to-service checks?
Are repeat failures subject to meaningful analysis and verification of lasting corrective action?
Are contractor test records held in accessible ACE-controlled repositories?
Are spare substitutions traced to technical equivalence decisions and quality records?
Does the maintenance dashboard distinguish safety-critical exceptions from aggregate completion performance?
Audit outcome classifications: Conforming, Partially Conforming, Nonconforming or Not Applicable; record sample reference, risk, owner, corrective action and independent verification.

docs.author: Ryan Ramsaran — Technical Writer / Procedures Specialist
docs.custodian: Ryan Ramsaran — Technical Writer / Procedures Specialist

docs.applies: All ACE-operated facilities, wells, shore-base activities, projects, contractors and organisational changes that could affect operational risk
docs.subtitle: Mandatory workflow to identify, assess, approve, implement, verify and close changes across ACE assets, organisations and documents.

blocks.t: This procedure establishes a single record of control for proposed changes that could alter hazards, risk barriers, asset configuration, operating limits, competence or obligations at ACE. It applies before change is authorised, during implementation, and until evidence of readiness and final close-out has been recorded.
No change affecting safety, environment, integrity, reliability, production or compliance shall be implemented until the MOC has been screened, risk-assessed and approved under this procedure.

The initiator owns the description and factual baseline; the Area Authority owns the safety of the operating location; the Technical Authority owns technical acceptability in the relevant discipline. Those decision rights are distinct and cannot substitute for one another.

The process covers permanent and temporary modifications to Pommerac A, Chenet B, Sapodilla C, offshore pipelines, Tamarind, Pawpaw and Soursop leases, the CPF, Point Lisas Shore Base, and associated offshore and land logistics. It also covers changes introduced through projects, vendors, contract services and shared facilities where ACE carries the resulting risk.

rows: Equipment substitutions; tie-ins; valve sizing; instrumentation; alarms; setpoints; protection logic; electrical classifications.
Feed composition; pressure, temperature, throughput or inventory changes; operating or safe operating limit revisions.
Shift numbers; critical roles; supervision; reporting lines; competence requirements; contractor operating responsibilities.
Operating procedures; isolations; maintenance strategies; inspection intervals; emergency arrangements; drawings and software.
Jetty, marine activity or flowline changes; access routes; shared facilities; interfaces to the Gas Buyer or partners.

blocks.t: Replacement in kind (RIK) is an exchange that preserves the approved design intent, performance, operating envelope, materials compatibility, interfaces and reliability. Equal catalogue appearance is insufficient: the initiator confirms manufacturer specification, certification, process compatibility and test arrangements against the authorised baseline.

A replacement shall be treated as a change if any essential design characteristic, duty, control function, protection layer, material, software configuration, operating limit or competence requirement differs or cannot be demonstrated equivalent.

rows: Design pressure, flow, capacity, range, material, certification and environmental rating match.
Raise MOC; relevant discipline TA review.
Connections, control logic, shutdown response, relief demand and alarm presentation remain unchanged.
Raise MOC; PSM screening and barrier review.
Spares, testing, maintenance and operator actions are equivalent and documented.
Raise MOC; maintenance and competence review.

blocks.t: When unsure whether a proposal is RIK, submit it for MOC screening. The screening decision and supporting comparison are retained; verbal acceptance is not a control.

Routine work conducted wholly within approved operating limits and unchanged procedures is governed by Control of Work rather than MOC. Repair of existing equipment with documented RIK is governed by maintenance work control. These exclusions cease to apply where the proposed activity changes the approved basis or introduces a new material hazard.
A work permit, purchase order, task risk assessment or engineering drawing approval shall not be accepted as a substitute for an MOC approval.
ACE-RSK-STD-001 Risk Management Standard; ACE-PSM-STD-001 Process Safety and Hazard Study Standard; ACE-COW-STD-001 Control of Work Standard; ACE-MNT-STD-001 Maintenance Management Standard.
1. The initiator records the business or safety need, originating problem, proposed solution, affected equipment or process, asset tag numbers, drawings, location and desired operating date.

2. The initiator identifies the approved baseline: operating envelope, P&IDs, cause-and-effect, equipment specifications, risk studies, permits, procedures, maintenance plans and personnel/competence arrangements.
3. Document Control or the MOC Coordinator assigns a unique MOC reference and enters it in the controlled MOC register before technical review begins.
4. The Area Authority determines whether any work or operating exposure is already under way and imposes immediate controls where needed.

The initiating record shall include MOC number, asset and equipment IDs, initiator, accountable change owner, current-state evidence, proposed-state description, drivers, requested date, change class, and linked risk/control records.

The accountable Manager, in consultation with the Area Authority and affected Technical Authorities, classifies scope and required review effort. The class governs process rigor; it does not downgrade the ACE Risk Matrix rating or replace technical approval.

rows: Small bounded change within a demonstrated, established design envelope; no new SCE function or major accident scenario.
Documented screening, focused risk review, affected TA agreement as applicable, manager and Area Authority release.
Modifies plant configuration, operating limits, procedures, interfaces, competence or safety-critical support arrangements.
Multi-discipline risk assessment, technical endorsement, defined implementation/PSSR and management approval.
Credible major accident hazard effect; new or materially altered SCE; major project tie-in; changed shutdown or relief philosophy.
Formal hazard-study selection, process safety lead review, TLC technical challenge where required, VP risk decision and rigorous PSSR.

blocks.t: Changes shall be classified by their most significant credible impact; splitting a large change into smaller requests shall not bypass the necessary study or authority.

rows: Could a new hazard or major accident scenario arise?
PSM review; HAZID, HAZOP or LOPA trigger decision.
Are any safety-critical barriers changed, bypassed or made unavailable?
SCE Register, performance standard and impairment control.
Are equipment integrity or design assumptions altered?
Process, mechanical, electrical, instrument, corrosion and structural TA review.
Do operating limits, procedures or emergency scenarios change?
Operations, EMR and training/document change action.
Are environmental permissions, Gas Buyer interfaces or partner obligations affected?
Environmental, legal, commercial and partner reviews.
Will people, roles, supervision or competence change?
Human Resources and operations competence plan.
Is software or OT instrumentation changed?
OT cyber/change baseline, backup and restoration plan.

blocks.t: The MOC Coordinator shall not advance an incomplete screening package to approval; unresolved screening questions are recorded as open actions with accountable owners.

The team assesses the current state, change activity (including construction, commissioning and transitional modes), and the proposed operating state separately. Use the approved ACE 5×5 qualitative matrix for current and residual risk. Assess credible health, safety, environment, asset, financial and reputation consequences using the governing consequence category.

An MOC shall carry a documented risk assessment that identifies initiating events, assumptions, existing safeguards, barrier dependencies, additional controls, residual risk and the role authorised to accept that risk.

The study is multi-disciplinary where the change crosses technical boundaries. Hold a structured design review for C2 changes and a formal hazard study for C3 where required by the Process Safety Lead. Record attendance, competency, references, scenario IDs and decisions, not only an unsigned risk score.

sections.title: 3.2 Review of risk barriers and safety-critical elements

blocks.t: Review bow-ties, SCE performance standards, demand modes, bypass arrangements, test intervals, common-cause vulnerabilities, operator response, utilities and emergency response interfaces. Identify both barriers modified by the change and existing barriers exposed during installation.
Any modification to an SCE, its performance standard, control logic or impairment status shall be reviewed and endorsed by the relevant Technical Authority before change approval.
An intended protective function is not a credited barrier until its design requirements, test/inspection evidence, operating dependency and owner have been verified for the proposed state.
Technical Authority: Validates design basis, codes, protection function, technical specification, testing and concessions within the affected discipline.
Process Safety Lead: Selects or endorses the hazard study method; challenges major accident scenarios, barrier assumptions and recommendations.
Area Authority: Validates operational readiness, SIMOPS, workforce availability, work authorisation, handover and local emergency response arrangements.
MOC owner: Resolves interface actions and integrates TA comments into one controlled implementation package.

Where several disciplines are implicated, the Manager, Technical Excellence coordinates an integrated review; unresolved significant differences are recorded and escalated through the Technical Leadership Council rather than concealed in a consensus notation.
Hazard-study and technical-review actions shall have a unique reference, named owner, verification evidence, due date, risk ranking, closure criterion and documented reviewer decision.

rows: Must be fully closed and independently verified before energisation, introduction of hydrocarbons or release of changed operation.
Must be closed before the work stage to which the requirement relates.
May remain open only when documented risk assessment, owner, due date and explicit approver acceptance show no impairment of required barriers.

blocks.t: 1. Change owner confirms completeness and identifies approving managers for the change scope.
2. Discipline Technical Authorities sign technical endorsements and outstanding conditions.
3. Area Authority agrees site risk, operating window, work interfaces and PSSR requirements.
4. The appropriate risk acceptance authority signs the residual risk decision under ACE-RSK-STD-001.
5. The accountable change approver authorises implementation; the MOC Coordinator changes status to Approved for implementation.
Work shall not be released based on the presence of a signed MOC alone: the specific work-control, permits, isolations and pre-start-up gates must also be satisfied.

rows: Design and barrier basis demonstrated; deviations identified.
Work window, permits, SIMOPS, staffing, operating restrictions.
Function Manager or Area Authority / L3
Control and action plan; specified operating conditions.
TA endorsement, written ALARP case, restrictions, dated reduction plan.
Stop or prevent exposure; CEO exceptional recovery decision only, not permission for ordinary operation.

blocks.t: Procedure ownership and approval authority are separate: Elena Farfan approves this procedure and ensures its consistent application; the accountable operating/project management and risk authority approve individual changes under the matrix above.

An MOC shall not be used to authorise departure from a mandatory ACE engineering or operating requirement. A separate deviation or exemption under ACE-OMS-STD-002 is required where such departure is proposed.

Typical mandatory hold points are design freeze, procurement release, isolation readiness, fabrication acceptance, testing completion, PSSR, operational release and close-out. Any conditions imposed by an approval become controlled action items in the MOC register.

The work pack links the approved change description to drawings, material specifications, vendor data, risk assessment, isolation plan, SIMOPS review, inspection/test plans, competence requirements, work-control documents, contingency arrangements and a clear restoration or rollback strategy when relevant.

Each authorised change shall have an implementation plan identifying work stages, inspection and test points, required records, accountable persons, contingency arrangements and pre-start-up acceptance criteria.

rows: Approved P&ID, SLD, cause-and-effect, specification or code update.
Permit pack, isolations, QA records, hold-point signatures.
Asset register, CMMS task changes, inspection/test requirements.
Procedure revisions, shift briefings, competency sign-off.
Response plan, notifications, regulatory or partner approvals.
Superseded controlled drawings, final redlines and source revision links.

blocks.t: Work executed before full commissioning can temporarily remove protection, create isolation boundaries or expose persons to live plant. The owner plans these phases explicitly and ensures that relevant permits and simultaneous operations controls refer to the correct temporary configuration.

Where work affects an active barrier, the job is held until the impairment risk is assessed, compensating safeguards are specified, the required deviation is approved and the Area Authority confirms the site can safely execute the work.

Controlled procedures, drawings, equipment data, operating limits, maintenance plans, training material and emergency instructions shall be updated before the changed activity is handed over for routine operation.

Communicate the changed operating envelope to relevant shifts, contractors, instrument/electrical and mechanical maintainers, and control rooms. Record the roster of affected roles, briefings, assessed competence and any short-duration interim instructions.

Implementation evidence includes drawing revisions, vendor and test certificates, change work orders, meeting minutes, training/competence records, operating-crew handovers and the formal PSSR dossier.

Pre-start-up safety review (PSSR) verifies that the approved design has been installed, construction and testing records support safe operation, competent people are ready, and new or modified barriers meet their performance standards. The degree of formality is based on change class and consequence.

rows: Installation, identification, inspection, as-builts and completion certificates.
ESD, fire and gas, relief, isolation, bypass controls and relevant proof tests.
Operating limits, commissioning medium, sequencing, hazard study action closure.
Approved operating instructions, training, supervision, emergency readiness.
Contractor handover, partner controls, Gas Buyer sales interface where affected, maintenance and spares.
PSSR checklist, punch-list ranking, endorsed exceptions, controlled release record.

sections.title: 6.2 Acceptance, punch list and controlled release

blocks.t: No process or equipment modification shall be placed in service until all safety-critical PSSR findings and required barrier tests are closed and the Area Authority has signed release to start.

Any residual punch item carried into operation must be demonstrated not to compromise required barriers, have a named owner and date, and be accepted by the change approver and Area Authority; critical items are not deferrable.
1. Close and verify pre-start-up findings; record evidence and independent verification where required.
2. Confirm management of temporary configurations, open isolations and inhibited systems.
3. Confirm that revised documents and competence/briefings are available to each operating shift.
4. Area Authority signs plant release; the MOC Coordinator records the actual start-up date and activation of post-start-up monitoring.

For changes with significant process or safety effects, define enhanced surveillance such as alarm trends, leak checks, product quality, vibration, instrument diagnostics or operator rounds during the first operating interval. Confirm expected performance against baseline assumptions and refer deviations to a new MOC or incident response as necessary.

Temporary changes create a defined departure from the baseline and may become normalised unless visibly registered. A temporary MOC states its start condition, permitted configuration, limits, expiry, compensating safeguards, named owner, restoration steps and test of successful restoration.
Every temporary change shall carry an expiry date and a restoration or permanent-conversion plan; it shall be reviewed before expiry and shall not be allowed to lapse into unapproved operation.

The default maximum initial approval period is 90 days. An extension requires a fresh risk and barrier review, affected TA endorsement and the original level of change approval. Repeated extensions require escalation to the relevant VP and a plan to eliminate the temporary configuration.
Measure: expired temporary MOCs in service — target zero; ageing temporary changes and repeat extensions reviewed monthly by Technical Excellence and the asset owner.

An emergency is an immediate threat requiring intervention to make plant or personnel safe. The Area Authority may order a shutdown or other protective action without awaiting an administrative approval. Resumption or design modification still requires a recorded change review commensurate with the time and risk available.

Emergency change classification is not a shortcut for production pressure, a late project or lack of planning. It is limited to protecting people, environment or asset integrity against an immediate credible threat.

An emergency modification that remains in service shall be entered in the MOC register as soon as the situation is stabilised and shall undergo formal technical and risk review before continued normal service is authorised.

Restoration to the baseline includes functional testing, revised drawings or configuration backups, cancellation of temporary constraints, removal of signage, shift handover, and close-out of linked deviation controls. The Area Authority verifies restoration before normal operation resumes.
1. Reconcile approved scope with installed configuration and any field variations; capture further changes as separate MOCs when necessary.
2. Complete remaining non-critical actions; verify that technical endorsements and risk controls are not merely signed but demonstrably effective.
3. Confirm final as-built drawings, asset data, SCE performance standards, CMMS plans, operations manuals, vendor information and training records are published and controlled.
4. Obtain acceptance from Area Authority and relevant TA; close the register record, retaining links to the originating work orders and hazard-study actions.
The MOC shall remain open until configuration records and defined close-out evidence are complete, or any justified carryover is controlled as a separate approved action with an accountable owner.

sections.title: 8.2 Reporting, overdue control and independent assurance

blocks.t: Monthly MOC scorecard: numbers submitted/approved/implemented/closed; overdue approvals; temporary changes past expiry (target zero); changes with PSSR complete; technical actions overdue; close-out within 90 days of start-up; changes started without approval (target zero).

The MOC Coordinator reports ageing and exception trends monthly to the Manager, Technical Excellence. The OMS Manager reviews systemic performance and audit findings. Relevant VPs receive overdue High-risk actions and barriers, with a corrective-action plan and due dates.

Designated discipline lead accountable for technical standards and endorsements.

sections.title: E.1 CPF separator pressure transmitter replacement

blocks.t: The CPF requires replacement of a pressure transmitter used by a shutdown function. The proposed instrument has a different span and firmware. It is not replacement in kind even if connections match: accuracy, trip configuration, proof testing and operator display can be affected. The MOC owner links the cause-and-effect sheet and performance standard, consults the Instrumentation and Process Safety TAs, tests the complete shutdown path, then secures PSSR and Area Authority release.

sections.title: E.2 Pommerac A temporary production configuration

blocks.t: An offshore process unit is proposed to operate for a limited period with a non-critical auxiliary arrangement changed while repairs proceed. Screening identifies a possible dependence on an SCE. The change cannot be authorised simply as temporary: the current barrier condition, deviation, alternate controls, expiry and restoration plan are reviewed. If risk remains Very High, routine operation is not authorised.

sections.title: E.3 Land lease field-crew organisation change

blocks.t: The Land Operations Manager proposes to combine supervisory coverage across Tamarind and Pawpaw leases. The MOC reviews response time, lone working, call-out, competence, communications and emergency cover. It may proceed only with an operational risk assessment and revised duty roster; no plant hardware drawing is needed to establish this as a change.

sections.title: Appendix G — Reference hierarchy and compliance check

blocks.t: Read this procedure with the currently approved ONE Risk Matrix, Process Safety Standard, Control of Work Standard, operating limits and any asset-specific engineering or well requirements. Where codes or regulation impose stricter requirements, comply with those requirements and refer any uncertainty to Legal & Government Affairs and the applicable TA. ONE tags and semantic paragraphs support navigation and do not diminish the authority of approved controlled sources.

The following test cases are used by Technical Excellence, Document Control and the ONE publishing/audit team to challenge correct interpretation of this procedure. They are not authorisations for the scenarios described; each actual change requires its own documented assessment.

sections.title: I.1 Workflow boundaries for the ONE portal

blocks.t: The ONE implementation should expose the MOC record through the linked risk register, SCE ID, affected Word section bookmarks, discipline owners, asset, change state and approval evidence. A user selecting an OMS 5.3 expectation must be able to navigate from this procedure to individual accountable roles and from an active MOC to the controlled documents it changes. A closed MOC remains read-only and is not silently deleted when the asset is decommissioned.

Changes to mandatory risk acceptance conditions, SCE requirements, safe operating limits or operating procedures shall trigger a review of affected document links before the revised configuration can be released.

Check that each approval refers to the final assessed design, not an obsolete option; the version of a referenced drawing is explicit; risk controls are executable and assigned; any performance test contains observed results; training covers the actual roles and shifts; and no post-start-up action has been misclassified as non-critical merely to avoid delaying commissioning.

sections.title: Appendix J — Temporal controls, escalation and quality audit

rows: Make safe; halt further change; escalate, investigate and register retrospective assessment without treating it as prior approval.
Notify and review before expiry; risk review and restoration or conversion decision.
Apply safe-state/restrictions; record deviation or breach; restore approved conditions.
Do not release the change; verify remedial evidence before re-review.
MOC closure older than 90 days after start-up
Review incomplete data, outstanding actions and escalation to asset manager.
Coach authors; check template controls, personnel, procedures and review resources.

blocks.t: Assurance sampling: each quarter sample at least one operational MOC from each operating area, one temporary change, a closed change and any high-consequence change, checking role approvals, technical basis, barrier controls, PSSR and record completeness.

The audit trail preserves every material version and decision. A change submitted, approved or closed by the same person without necessary independent technical review is an exception requiring documented governance challenge. The ONE portal should make expiry, status and unresolved barrier conditions visible to authorised users.

docs.title: Governance, Assurance and Continuous Improvement Policy
docs.author: Kwame Henry — Strategy & Planning Analyst
docs.custodian: Gary Ho Sing — Manager, Strategy & Planning
docs.reviewers: Gary Ho Sing — Manager, Strategy & Planning; Marissa Bobb — OMS Manager; Nicole Lange — Head of Internal Audit & Risk Assurance; Dillon Haddad — Compliance & Assurance Manager; George Habib — VP HSE & Compliance; Andrea Farfan — Learning & Competence Manager
docs.applies: All ACE activities, sites, employees and contractors
docs.subtitle: How ACE organises its work into processes, sets objectives, tests that ONE works and turns every improvement into proven, lasting change.

blocks.t: This policy sets how ACE steers and improves its management system: how work is organised into processes, how objectives are set, how assurance tests that ONE works, and how every improvement is raised, decided, proven and made permanent. It is the governing policy of the Continuous Improvement (CI) dimension in ONE.

It applies to every function and site (HOF, PLB, PAP, CHB, SAP, CPF and LND), to every L3 process in the Process Register (ACE-BPM-REG-001), and to contractors whose work forms part of an ACE process. Its parent is ACE-LDR-POL-001.
Each commitment names the ACE values it serves, as set in ACE-LDR-POL-001 section 1. The steps that deliver the commitments are in the governed processes and implementing documents in section 6.

In line with our value One team, one way, all ACE work is organised as L3 processes, each with exactly one owner, one primary function and one governing policy. Every corporate objective is carried by at least one process, so that no objective is left without a way of delivering it (ACE-BPM-PRA-001).

In line with our values One team, one way and Learn and improve, ACE sets its OMS objectives every year in an annual OMS plan. Each objective is measurable, has one owner, and is linked to the processes that deliver it and the risks it addresses.

Each annual objective shall be recorded in the Objectives and Opportunities register (OMS-REG-001) with a target, an owner, the linked processes and the linked risks before the start of the plan year.

In line with our values Integrity in everything and Safety above all, ACE tests whether its controls and processes work in the field through three lines: checks by the line, conformance assessments by the OMS team, and independent audit by Internal Audit. The annual assurance plan is risk-based and every one of the ten OMS elements is independently audited at least once in every three-year period (ACE-PRF-STD-002).

In line with our value Learn and improve, improving how we work is part of every job, not an extra. Every improvement is tied to the process it improves and, where possible, to the step in that process, so that ONE can show where improvement is happening and where it is not.
Every improvement item shall be recorded in the CI register against one L3 process and, where it can be identified, one process step.
In line with our values Learn and improve and One team, one way, ACE takes improvements from five sources, and anyone may raise one:
Incident and near-miss actions, from investigations under ACE-INC-STD-001.
Audit and assurance findings, from all three lines of assurance.
Process reviews: the annual review and trigger reviews of each process.
KPI breaches: a process KPI outside its target for two consecutive periods.
Staff ideas, which any employee or contractor may raise at any time.
These five sources are the values of the source field in the CI register.
In line with our value Learn and improve, the effort spent on an improvement matches its size and risk. ACE uses four routes, which are the values of the method field in the CI register:
Just do it: within one function, low risk, and no change to roles, controls or systems.
PDCA (Plan, Do, Check, Act): an improvement led by the process owner within the process.
DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve, Control): a data-driven study for a cross-functional problem or a KPI breach.
Project: an improvement that needs capital, or a change classed C3 under ACE-MOC-PRC-001.
The process owner chooses the route and escalates to the BPM system owner when the right route is unclear or the improvement crosses process boundaries. Section 4 sets who approves each route.

In line with our values Integrity in everything and Learn and improve, an improvement is judged by evidence, not by opinion. An item reaches the Verified stage only when a measured KPI has moved against its recorded baseline, or a control has been shown to work by a test or an assurance check.
An improvement item shall not be closed until its benefit has been verified against a recorded baseline KPI or a demonstrated control test.

In line with our value One team, one way, a verified improvement becomes the normal way of working. Changes to wording and step detail are made by document revision; changes to roles, controls or systems are made through Management of Change (C-BPM-044 in ACE-BPM-PRA-003). An item reaches the Standardised stage when the revised document or the MOC is approved and the people in each affected lane have been briefed.

In line with our values Learn and improve and One team, one way, ACE recognises improvements and the people behind them, including staff and contractors who raise ideas. Recognition is visible on the ONE improvement board and in leadership communication, and it is fair and consistent across functions and sites.

In line with our value Learn and improve, ACE processes become more mature over time. Our target is that every Current process reaches maturity Level 3 (Managed) or above on the scale in ACE-BPM-PRA-003 by the end of 2028.

sections.title: 2.11 Leadership review of the whole system

blocks.t: In line with our values One team, one way and Learn and improve, the Executive Leadership Team steps back once a year to ask whether ONE still works, still suits ACE and is becoming more mature, and sets the improvement priorities for the next annual plan.

rows: Owns this policy; chairs the annual management review; approves the annual OMS plan.
Manager, Strategy & Planning (BPM system owner, custodian)
Owns the process architecture and the CI register; decides escalated CI routes; owner of the BPM processes and of the Improvement Management Process.
Head of Internal Audit & Risk Assurance
Owns the independent assurance plan and the three-year element coverage.
Runs conformance assessments and the annual OMS maturity assessment; prepares the management review.
Owner of the Audit Planning and Follow-up Process (ACE-PRF-PRS-001); samples process conformance and maturity.
Ensures process owners are trained and lane roles are briefed after a change.
Own the improvement of their processes; choose the CI route; decide on ideas raised against their process.
Receive quarterly process KPI reports; approve DMAIC studies in their function.

blocks.t: The BPM system owner shall maintain the CI register and report its status to the Executive Leadership Team twice a year.

docs.title: Deviation and Exemption Standard
docs.author: Marissa Bobb — OMS Manager
docs.reviewers: Elena Farfan — Manager, Technical Excellence; Damian Daniel — Process Safety Lead; Dillon Haddad — Compliance & Assurance Manager
docs.applies: All ACE assets, activities, employees, contractors and managed interfaces
docs.subtitle: Risk-based control of departures from mandatory requirements, including safety-critical barrier impairments.

blocks.t: This standard governs the decision to depart temporarily from a requirement in an ACE policy, standard, procedure, work instruction or approved technical specification. It also governs requests to exempt a defined asset or activity from a non-statutory requirement when full compliance is not practicable and a formal, durable alternative control is proposed. It applies equally to ACE employees, contractors and controlled interfaces with joint venture partners.

Any departure from a mandatory ACE requirement shall be identified, risk-assessed, endorsed and approved before the affected work starts or continues, except immediate protective actions necessary to make a situation safe.

A deviation approval shall identify the precise requirement affected, the approved alternative, a named owner, the affected asset and operating envelope, monitoring, review and an unambiguous expiry or termination condition.
The approved requirement remains in force for all other work and locations. Approval for one deviation shall not be used as precedent or permission for unrelated departures.
Do not treat an expired approval, contractor method statement, permit to work, verbal instruction or email conversation as authority to depart from a mandatory requirement.

The risk-management rules in ACE-RSK-STD-001 govern risk ratings and acceptance authorities. Technical integrity is governed by ACE-AIM-STD-001. Approved changes to plant, people or procedures are managed under ACE-MOC-PRC-001. This standard connects these controls but does not replace them.
Deviation: a controlled and time-limited departure from an applicable ACE mandatory requirement, with specified boundaries, compensating safeguards, approval and expiry.

Exemption: a formally authorized exception to a defined non-statutory company requirement for a specific asset, activity or configuration, supported by a documented equivalent or superior means of meeting its underlying intent.

A normal technical choice made within an approved standard is not a deviation. A replacement in kind that meets all specifications is not a deviation. An alternative explicitly permitted in a standard is not a deviation when all stated conditions are met.
The initiator shall identify the relevant paragraph, drawing, performance-standard clause or operating limit and state exactly why the proposed arrangement would not meet it.

A standing or permanent exemption shall be recorded as a controlled variance with a review trigger and shall be progressed through management of change and revision of the affected technical baseline; an indefinite temporary deviation is not permitted.

Examples include a failed safety-critical proof test on Pommerac A, a required inspection or maintenance task that cannot be completed by its due date, a temporary operating configuration at the Central Processing Facility, a substitute material whose specification differs from the approved design, and a contractor procedure that conflicts with an ACE mandatory requirement.
Where there is doubt whether a requirement is mandatory, the initiator shall seek a determination from the document owner and relevant Technical Authority before treating it as optional.
The Area Authority shall maintain control of the affected equipment or work while a proposed deviation is assessed, including applying temporary restrictions or stopping work when necessary.

sections.title: 1.3 Actions that cannot be authorised by this standard

blocks.t: A deviation or exemption shall not purport to waive legislation, a licence condition, a regulator's direction, a third-party contractual consent, an absolute safe operating limit or an approved prohibition on bypassing a critical safeguard.
Proposed departures affecting a legal or permit obligation shall be referred to Legal & Government Affairs and the regulatory compliance owner before any decision to implement.
Where a law, permit or absolute engineering limit cannot be met, stop or prevent the activity. Obtain the external authorization or restore compliance; an internal exception has no legal force.
Commercial urgency, an unavailable spare, reduced staffing or a missed planning window are not by themselves reasons to accept unacceptable risk.

sections.title: 1.4 Discovery during work or in an emergency

blocks.t: On discovery of an unapproved departure, the person in charge shall secure the activity, inform the Area Authority and preserve the evidence needed to reconstruct the condition.
The responsible manager shall initiate incident or non-conformance reporting when loss of control, an unplanned barrier impairment or a breach of mandatory control has occurred.

Immediate actions to protect life, isolate hazardous energy or stabilise a plant are emergency-response measures, not retrospective approval of unsafe work. Any continued impaired state is assessed under this standard before planned operations resume.
ACE-INC-STD-001 — Incident Reporting and Investigation Standard.
The initiator shall submit a deviation request through the controlled ONE register before the planned departure is implemented.

The request shall state the affected facility or equipment tag, document and clause, nature and reason for non-compliance, first exposure date, proposed end date, requested operating restrictions, and the person who will own the condition.
The initiator shall identify other open deviations, work orders, permits, MOC records, risk register items and recent incidents relevant to the same equipment, barrier or operating system.
The approved request, supporting analysis, consultation, approval decisions, restrictions and closure evidence shall be retained as a controlled deviation record.

sections.title: 2.2 Assess the actual risk and proposed alternative

blocks.t: The assessment shall use the consequence descriptions and likelihood categories in the ACE Risk Matrix, identify the credible worst affected consequence domain and record both current and proposed residual risk.
The assessment shall distinguish safeguards that are already functioning from measures that are proposed but not yet installed or verified; proposed safeguards receive no credit until tested.
A High or Very High risk shall be escalated under ACE-RSK-STD-001, with ALARP justification and acceptance at the required level, before any decision on continued exposure.

Consider common-cause failures, dependent barriers, the length of exposure, demand frequency, operating mode, weather and marine access, competence, simultaneous operations, and the ability to detect deterioration.

Where the risk may be sensitive to assumptions, record the assumptions, evidence and sensitivity. Where credible uncertainty is material, use a conservative classification until further verification resolves it.

sections.title: 2.3 Technical Authority endorsement and specialist review

blocks.t: Technical deviations shall be reviewed by the discipline Technical Authority responsible for the affected standard or performance requirement.

A deviation affecting a major accident hazard, protective instrumented function, well barrier, containment boundary, structural integrity or emergency response capability shall receive Process Safety review where relevant and explicit consideration of the major accident bow-tie.

The Technical Authority evaluates the engineering acceptability of the proposed alternative and records any non-negotiable technical limits; the Area Authority confirms whether those limits can actually be maintained at the worksite.
Cross-discipline impacts may require the Technical Leadership Council to coordinate endorsements. The Council's endorsement does not substitute for the risk-based approval authority.
Before submission for approval, the owner shall prepare an executable plan naming each temporary measure, its verifier, due date, evidence and method of ongoing monitoring.

Controls shall include alarm or surveillance arrangements, work restrictions, permit and isolation implications, contingency response, communication to affected shifts and contractors, and a defined recovery action.
Temporary operating instructions shall identify which regular procedure steps are suspended, which remain mandatory and what work must stop if the alternative control fails.

Do not count a manual watch, additional inspection or procedural instruction as equivalent to an automatic protective function without competent engineering evidence addressing response time and reliability.
ACE-COW-STD-001 — Control of Work Standard.

No approval decision shall be recorded as valid unless the request identifies the requirement, the affected boundary, current and residual risk, time limit, alternatives considered, endorsements, approver and owner.
The OMS Manager or delegated register custodian shall return incomplete requests for correction and shall prevent an unapproved request from appearing as active or authorized in ONE.
A rejected request remains in the audit trail with its rationale. The originator may resubmit a revised proposal with new evidence; rejection is not erased.

The minimum person authorised to accept residual risk shall be determined from the current and proposed residual risk ratings under ACE-RSK-STD-001; a deviation may demand a higher authority based on its technical significance.

Low residual risk requires acceptance by the accountable Supervisor or L4 Lead; Medium by the Function Manager or Area Authority (L3); High by the relevant Vice President (L2); Very High is not acceptable as routine operation and is escalated to the CEO only for exceptional recovery decisions.
Technical Authority endorsement shall be obtained independently of managerial acceptance where an engineering standard, safety-critical element or technical limit is affected.

The approver shall record acceptance of the defined residual risk, scope and conditions; approval of risk does not override independent authorization for permits, MOC, isolation, legal conditions or technical hold points.
A higher-level approver may make a more restrictive decision than the minimum authority. An approver may reject a deviation even when the rating permits consideration.
An approved deviation shall not become effective until all controls marked as preconditions are implemented and verified by a named independent checker appropriate to the risk.
The Area Authority shall acknowledge the approved conditions, brief the affected shifts, link the deviation to active permits and relevant work orders, and record the actual start of the departure.
The effective approval shall be available at the point of work or accessible through the controlled ONE record; references on permits alone are not sufficient.
Any change in location, equipment, operating mode, risk rating or scope shall trigger reassessment and, where material, a new approval before continued exposure.
The relevant function owner shall identify approvals from partners, clients, marine authorities, regulators or permit issuers where interfaces require them.
A contractor-proposed alternative shall be endorsed by ACE's responsible Technical Authority and accepted by the ACE Area Authority; contractor management approval alone is insufficient.

A deviation does not alter the contractor's contractual obligations or the applicable statutory requirements. Any lasting contract or engineering change follows the established commercial and MOC processes.
ACE-CON-STD-001 — Contractor and Supplier Management Standard (planned document).

Where the residual risk cannot be demonstrated tolerable, or the necessary safeguards cannot be verified, the approving authority shall refuse continued operation and require the affected activity to stop or remain isolated.
Disagreement between the Area Authority and Technical Authority on a safety-critical deviation shall be escalated to the relevant Vice President without releasing the hold.
Do not operate under a request marked Draft, In Review, Rejected, Expired or Closed. Only the approved active period and conditions authorize the defined exception.
Any failed, bypassed, degraded or unavailable safety-critical element shall be logged against its SCE Register entry and performance standard as soon as discovered.
The owner shall identify the threatened major accident hazard, failed performance function, affected prevention or mitigation barriers and the required maximum restoration priority.

The impairment assessment shall consider whether other barriers relied upon in the bow-tie are independent and effective, including common utilities, instrument air, electrical supply, communication and operator response.
ACE-AIM-STD-001 — Asset Integrity Management Standard.
ACE-AIM-REG-001 — Safety-Critical Element Register and Performance Standards (planned document).

Continued operation with an impaired safety-critical element shall require Technical Authority endorsement, risk-based management approval, confirmed interim controls and explicit Area Authority release.

The operating instruction shall state the permitted operating envelope, loading or production restrictions, alternative alarm and detection arrangements, test or inspection frequency and conditions that trigger immediate shutdown.
For emergency shutdown, fire and gas, pressure protection or well barriers, the assessment must address demand scenarios and whether alternative safeguards perform within the required response time.
Do not bypass or inhibit a safety-critical protective function merely to prevent nuisance trips or maintain production. Resolve the cause or use the full impairment and approval process.

sections.title: 4.3 Deferrals, overdue verification and cumulative risk

blocks.t: A deferral of a safety-critical inspection, test or maintenance activity shall be cross-referenced to the deviation and to the CMMS or inspection management record; approval of one record shall not silently extend another.
The owner shall review simultaneous or repeated impairments within the same major accident hazard and consider cumulative risk rather than rating each independently.
Repeat deferrals shall be reported as recurring degradation in the relevant integrity and assurance forums, with a recovery plan and escalation as needed.
The absence of a known incident during prior deferrals is not evidence that an impaired barrier is effective.
ACE-MNT-STD-001 — Maintenance Management Standard.

The restoration evidence shall demonstrate the function is returned to its approved performance standard, including the appropriate inspection, test, calibration, reinstatement and independent verification.

The Area Authority shall authorize return to normal operating conditions only after confirming that temporary measures and inhibits are removed, control documents are updated and the record is closed or formally transitioned.
Testing and reinstatement records, completed work orders and independent verification shall be retained with the deviation closure.
Every temporary deviation shall have a specific start and expiry date, a nominated monitoring interval and a target restoration or compliant-replacement milestone.
The selected expiry shall reflect consequence, exposure and available recovery options; it shall not be set merely to avoid review at a convenient reporting date.

Low-risk departures may be proposed for up to 180 days; Medium-risk departures up to 90 days; High-risk departures up to 30 days, unless a more restrictive technical or legal limit applies. These are maximum initial periods, not automatic entitlements.

A request outside the initial duration schedule shall be referred to the relevant Vice President and OMS Manager for explicit documented justification; High-risk duration relief also requires the original Technical Authority's endorsement.
No routine time allowance is defined for Very High risk because routine exposure is not permitted.
The owner shall request an extension sufficiently before expiry to permit reassessment, independent review and a decision without operating past the existing end date.
Extension requests shall include evidence of controls maintained, incidents or near misses, changes in cumulative risk, missed restoration milestones and a credible revised completion plan.
An extension shall be approved at the same or higher authority as the original risk acceptance, following renewed Technical Authority endorsement where applicable.

No more than one extension may be granted under the original deviation identifier; continuing need after that shall trigger a fresh, explicitly linked assessment, management review and a decision on permanent corrective action.
Do not allow automatic renewal. An approval expiring at midnight ceases at the stated local time unless a replacement approval is already effective.
The ONE register shall flag approaching expiry, and the deviation owner shall notify the Area Authority when restoration is at risk of missing the required date.

At expiry without a replacement authorization, affected work shall stop or equipment shall be placed into its pre-defined safe state. The exception record is marked Expired and remains visible as a non-conformance until resolved.
The owner shall initiate escalation and incident reporting where operation continued outside authorization or a barrier was knowingly left impaired.
The OMS Manager oversees expiry escalation; the Area Authority controls the physical work or operating state.
Closure shall identify what restored compliance, the evidence of testing or inspection, the date restrictions were removed and the persons who verified technical and operational acceptance.
For an exemption converted into a permanent approved design or procedure change, the MOC and revised controlling document shall be effective before the temporary deviation can be closed as resolved.
The Technical Authority shall verify return to the required performance basis where integrity or process safety was affected; the Area Authority verifies site status and communication.
The closed record shall retain the original approval and all extensions, decisions, changes and verification attachments for traceability.
All deviations and exemptions shall be recorded in the controlled ONE deviation register, with a unique persistent identifier and immutable history of status, approval and expiry changes.
The record shall link to the relevant standard clause, technical asset tag, risk assessment, impairment, MOC, incident, work order and permit as applicable.
The register shall identify the deviation owner and Area Authority, plus approver and Technical Authority where applicable; changes to named ownership must be recorded with effective date.
The OMS Manager maintains the register structure and data integrity; the individual deviation owner maintains the accuracy of conditions and progress at the worksite.
The owner shall verify controls at the frequency defined in the approval and shall record any failure or change in underlying risk immediately.

The OMS Manager shall provide a monthly dashboard showing open items by risk class and asset, SCE impairments, overdue and expiring approvals, extensions, repeated departures and restoration progress.
High-risk and safety-critical deviations shall be reviewed in the relevant asset or function risk meeting and escalated to the approving Vice President when recovery dates slip.

Key measures: overdue active deviations (target zero); approved items without verified preconditions (target zero); safety-critical impairment exposure days; extensions per asset; and closures with complete restoration evidence.
The Compliance & Assurance Manager shall sample open and closed deviation records for correct risk rating, independence of endorsement, expiry control and evidence of effective restoration.
System owners shall use recurring deviation causes to improve standards, planned maintenance, spares availability, engineering designs and workforce competence.
The purpose of the deviation process is to make a temporary weakness visible and controlled, not to normalize operation with degraded barriers.
ACE-PRF-STD-002 — Assurance and Audit Standard.
ACE-INC-STD-001 — Incident Reporting and Investigation Standard.

sections.title: Appendix D — Barrier and assessment checklist

rows: Is the exact binding clause identified, and are legal and contractual conditions separated?

What other work, inhibits, isolations, deferred tasks or contractors influence the risk?
What makes the requested exposure period necessary and acceptable?
What condition triggers stop, shutdown or an alternative safe operating mode?
What physical evidence proves that prerequisites are active and restoration is complete?

blocks.t: A completed checklist is evidence of review, not a substitute for the engineering assessment, bow-tie verification or competent risk acceptance.

sections.title: E.1 Pommerac A — temporary emergency shutdown valve impairment

blocks.t: A scheduled proof test discovers that an ESD valve cannot demonstrate the response required by its performance standard. The maintenance team stops the release of the valve to service and records the fault against the SCE Register and CMMS task.

The Area Authority confirms the affected isolation boundary and places the equipment in a safe operating state while the Process Safety Lead and relevant Technical Authority examine the bow-tie consequences, remaining independent layers, repair plan and whether continued exposure is tolerable.

If a controlled temporary configuration is considered, the owner requests a deviation stating production restrictions, alternate independent containment, alarm and surveillance measures, restoration deadline and explicit stop triggers. The VP accepts any High residual risk; the Area Authority only releases operation after preconditions are verified.
Failure to demonstrate an acceptable independent barrier results in continued shutdown. A production target does not change the decision.
The test report, risk evaluation, approval, shift briefings, repair work order and successful functional re-test form one retrievable closure record.

sections.title: E.2 Central Processing Facility — deferred critical inspection

blocks.t: An inspection of a corrosion-sensitive vessel is approaching its mandatory due date, but access is unavailable during normal production. The inspection lead checks whether the due date arises from law, an approved written scheme or an ACE risk-based programme.

Any legal inspection requirement is referred to Legal & Government Affairs for formal external resolution. For an internal programme requirement, the owner assesses remaining life, corrosion history, recent operating exposure and the alternatives for inspection or reduced operation.

A time-limited deviation may be considered with reduced operating limits, enhanced monitoring, an inspection plan and approval commensurate with residual risk. The CMMS deferral and integrity anomaly register are linked.
The closure bundle includes actual inspection findings, correction of the backlog, Technical Authority verification and removal of temporary restrictions.

sections.title: E.3 Point Lisas Shore Base — substitute critical component

blocks.t: A vendor proposes a component with different material specification because the stocked replacement is unavailable. The purchasing decision is held while the Technical Authority checks service conditions, corrosion compatibility, pressure rating and life-cycle implications.

If the alternative falls within the published standard's permitted options, no deviation is needed; the approved technical equivalency is recorded in procurement. If it conflicts with a mandatory clause, the request identifies the clause and technical justification and considers MOC.
Vendor assurance and a purchase order do not authorize an engineering deviation.
The approved selection basis, QA record, inspection and receipt certification remain linked to the equipment technical file.

sections.title: E.4 Land-lease work — simultaneous activities conflict

blocks.t: A workover crew proposes lifting operations during a planned pipeline isolation at the Pawpaw lease. The Area Authority identifies an interface conflict with the SIMOPS plan and an ACE work-control requirement.

The first option is to change the schedule and comply. Where an alternative work arrangement is proposed, the performing authorities assess the combined risk, exclusion zones, communications and shared emergency arrangements before requesting a controlled departure.
Any acceptance of the combined arrangement requires the proper risk authority and release through the control-of-work process. The deviation itself is not a permit.
The approved SIMOPS matrix, revised work pack, toolbox briefs and reinstatement are retained.

sections.title: E.5 Licence condition — exemption not permitted

blocks.t: A planned operation cannot meet a permit condition applicable to its discharge or reporting arrangements. The operation is not made compliant by an ACE manager approving a local exemption.
Do not proceed on the strength of an internal waiver. Secure a lawful change to the permit through the competent authority or revise the activity to meet the existing condition.
Legal & Government Affairs shall be consulted where the condition or regulator authorization is uncertain.
The regulatory correspondence and updated approved basis form the legal compliance record.

docs.title: Operating Envelopes and Integrity Operating Windows Practice
docs.author: Michelle de Verteuil — Process Engineering Lead

docs.subtitle: Methods for defining, approving, monitoring and responding to operating limits and integrity operating windows across ACE facilities.

blocks.t: This Practice establishes the engineering and operating method used to define, classify, document, monitor and respond to operating limits and Integrity Operating Windows (IOWs). It provides the technical bridge between design intent, process safety analysis, materials and corrosion knowledge, operating discipline and integrity management. It applies to the Central Processing Facility (CPF), Pommerac A (PAP), land leases (LND), and interfaces with offshore unmanned facilities and supporting logistics. The Practice serves ACE-OPS-STD-001 Operating Envelopes and Operating Limits Standard and does not replace Control of Work, Risk Management, Management of Change or Asset Integrity requirements.

Recognised practice applied: API RP 584 Integrity Operating Windows; IEC 62682 Management of alarm systems for the process industries; IEC 61511 Functional safety — safety instrumented systems for the process industry sector.

rows: Approves operating-limit framework and critical operating restrictions; accountable for operating discipline.
Michelle de Verteuil — Process Engineering Lead
Maintains methodology, technical basis and limit register quality; coordinates reviews.
Rohan Ali — Plant Manager - Central Processing Facility
Implements CPF limits, alarm response and shift communication.
Arjun Gittens — Offshore Operations Manager (Gulf of Paria)

blocks.t: The Process Engineering Lead shall maintain the Operating Limits Register and the technical basis dossier for every limit in it.
The Production Chemistry Lead shall set and review the chemistry IOWs, including corrosion inhibitor injection rates, with the Materials & Corrosion Lead.
Limits are nested; lower-level targets never override an upper-level safety or integrity boundary.

blocks.t: Every IOW shall be classified as critical, standard or informational using the hierarchy above, and the class shall be shown in the register and on the control room display (C-OPS-001).

Limit-setting uses a documented technical basis rather than historical convenience. The owner assembles design basis, equipment datasheets, HAZOP/LOPA actions, operating experience, fluid properties, corrosion studies, materials selection, process chemistry, instrument capability and applicable codes. The limit is challenged for normal, startup, shutdown, upset and degraded conditions. Conflicting constraints are resolved by applying the most conservative applicable boundary until the technical authority documents the resolution.

rows: Confirm units, allowable range and operating modes.

blocks.t: Each limit shall have a technical basis dossier that records the evidence in the table above and is approved by the relevant Technical Authority before the limit is published (C-OPS-002).
Where two constraints conflict, the more conservative boundary shall apply until the Technical Authority records a resolution (C-OPS-003).

Each limit shall be recorded in the Operating Limits Register with a unique identifier, explicit units and enough context for ONE and the control room display to show the approved boundary and response.

blocks.t: A limit shall not be published until it has an accountable owner, a technical approver, a monitoring method and a response instruction (C-OPS-004).
Alarm and trip settings in the control system shall be reconciled with the Operating Limits Register every six months by the Instrumentation & Control Lead (C-OPS-005).
Excursions are assessed by limit class, magnitude, duration, trend and consequence. Where uncertainty exists, treat the event as the more severe class pending assessment.

blocks.t: A sustained, repeated or unexplained excursion may indicate a barrier failure, ineffective safeguard or process drift. Apply Incident Reporting and Investigation and Deviation and Exemption requirements when their thresholds are met. Do not create an informal tolerance by repeated reset or acknowledgement.
Operators shall respond to a critical IOW excursion with the approved immediate action and notify the Area Authority and Technical Authority within one hour (C-OPS-006).
A standard IOW excursion that lasts longer than its duration allowance, or recurs three times in 30 days, shall be reported in the incident system under ACE-INC-STD-001 (C-OPS-007).
Repeated excursions shall not be normalised by resetting or acknowledging alarms; target values shall not be used in place of approved limits (C-OPS-008).

Temporary limits have an expiry and a named accountable owner. Review follows incidents, process changes, equipment modification, chemistry change, inspection findings, study revisions or material trend shifts.
Operating limits shall only be changed through ACE-MOC-PRC-001, and the MOC shall identify the technical basis, affected modes, alarms and trips, procedures, training and registers (C-OPS-009).
A change to a critical IOW shall be endorsed by the relevant Technical Authority and approved by the VP Operations.
The Process Engineering Lead and Materials & Corrosion Lead shall hold a quarterly IOW review of excursion trends and record decisions and actions (C-OPS-010).

Leading: critical IOW excursions acknowledged within one hour (target 100%); IOW reviews held on schedule (target 100%); register-to-DCS mismatches (target 0). Lagging: integrity damage attributed to an IOW excursion.

docs.title: Operating Envelopes and Operating Limits Standard
docs.author: Michelle de Verteuil — Process Engineering Lead
docs.custodian: Michelle de Verteuil — Process Engineering Lead
docs.reviewers: Rohan Ali — Plant Manager - Central Processing Facility; Arjun Gittens — Offshore Operations Manager (Gulf of Paria); Vijay Ramcharan — Instrumentation & Control Lead
docs.applies: All ACE operated facilities: CPF, Pommerac A, Chenet B, Sapodilla C, Gulf of Paria pipelines, Tamarind, Pawpaw and Soursop leases, and associated terminals and utilities
docs.subtitle: Safe operating boundaries, alarm response, exceedance management and change control for ACE production and processing assets.

blocks.t: The objective is to ensure that ACE facilities remain within defined, technically justified limits throughout startup, steady production, planned shutdown, abnormal operation and recovery. An operating envelope translates design constraints, hazard assessments and equipment capability into parameters that operators can see and act upon.

The requirements cover the Central Processing Facility (CPF), offshore production and wellhead platforms, Gulf of Paria pipelines, land leases, the tank farm and loading operations. Facility-specific registers provide actual approved values; this standard defines how those values are established, maintained, communicated and verified. Neither a sample table nor a trend screenshot constitutes an approved operating limit.

Every operating facility shall maintain a current operating-envelope register with identified safety-critical, integrity and operational limits, assigned owners and an approved response for each credible exceedance.
Operating instructions, process displays, alarm rationalisation records and limit registers shall use the same approved operating boundary and revision identification.

When a limit is uncertain, inaccessible or contradicted by another source, operations shall adopt the more conservative safe condition, stop any activity that depends on the disputed limit and obtain the Area Authority and Process Engineering Lead decision before proceeding.
